rationale: Evidence: all three components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. The ordering of 15 minutes standard below 20 minutes UAM is correct and both are conservative relative to common defaults. However the configured cap does not bound delivered SMB in this build: at 08-19 16:54 local with a 0.5 U/h basal segment the 20-minute allowance implies roughly 0.17 units, yet the text records UAM High Boost enacted with SMB equals 1.6 units, and at 08-07 22:16 local standardMaxBolus 0.2 accompanies 0.4 units microbolused. Uncertainty: the boost multiplier is not present in decision_inventory and is not adjustable through any supplied field, so reducing the minutes value would scale boosted SMB by roughly a quarter but would not cap it; confidence in the size of the benefit is therefore limited. Dependencies: this group and max_iob both act on the same insulin exposure, and the rule against changing dependent settings together means only one may move per observation window. max_iob is prioritised because it is a pure ceiling with no effect on routine dosing, so this group is kept this cycle and flagged as the sequence-position-two candidate.

Evidence: both components are non-null, so verify is not permissible and change is supported with explicit old and new values. max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is retained unchanged because it is demonstrably inert: the binding ceiling observed at 08-14 19:40 local is an adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, consistent with the 0.8 U/h peak profile basal and the daily safety multiplier of 5.0, and the highest temp basal seen anywhere is 3.6 to 4.0 U/h, so 12 U/h is never reached. max_iob_units changes from 25 U to 10 U because 25 units is roughly one full day of insulin or more against 16.2 units of scheduled basal per day and 275.95 units recorded over 14 days, and therefore never engages. The highest observed insulin on board is 5.935 units at 08-21 22:10 local, where the loop still requested 2.12 further units at 4 U/h with sensitivity at 27.8 mg/dL per unit and nothing in the configuration would have arrested accumulation; a second peak of 4.73 units occurred at 08-19 16:55 local and was followed by minus 168 mg/dL over 120 minutes. A 10 unit ceiling sits well above the observed operating range, leaves routine days untouched, and engages only in the tail events that precede the level 2 readings of 41 to 48 mg/dL on 08-13, 08-14 and 08-21. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 device statuses are exposed so the true peak may exceed 5.935 units, and it is unresolved whether total_insulin_u includes temp basal delivery, which affects the true total daily dose scale; a conservative rather than tight ceiling is proposed for both reasons. Dependencies: this is the least entangled available lever because a ceiling does not interact with basal, carb ratio, ISF, DIA or target, which is why it is the single change of this cycle; it must not be combined with the SMB allowance, the dynamic sensitivity factor, DIA or any basal segment.

Evidence: all five components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. The configuration is internally coherent, with dynamic sensitivity enabled and Autosens disabled as the correct mutually exclusive pairing and the two Autosens target flags inert while Autosens is off. Sensitivity ratios of 0.79 to 1.0 in the sample were read as neutral-to-mildly-sensitive current adjustments from the dynamic path, not as evidence of Autosens activity, and 1.0 was explicitly not read as disabled. The substantive finding is dispersion with a feedback character: effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, and two statuses at nearly identical glucose, 124.1 and 135.1 mg/dL, showed 83.0 and 42.5 mg/dL per unit, implicating the rolling insulin term rather than glucose alone. Uncertainty: high, and the unresolved question of whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 includes temp basal directly scales how aggressive this feedback actually is. Dependencies: the 70 percent factor, DIA of 10 hours and the SMB boost all modulate the same quantity, so it cannot be moved in the same cycle as either; it is designated the third-cycle candidate after max_iob and after the DIA verification.

Evidence: both components are non-null, so verify is not permissible. Both settings act only on carbohydrates-on-board decay and absorption modelling, and carbohydrates on board are zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses with zero carb entries and zero extended carb entries across 14 days, so both are entirely inert and no observation in the package can support or refute either. Uncertainty: as a conditional note only, meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 matches the observed midday excursion length of roughly six to seven hours well, while min_5m_carbimpact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes implies a fast minimum absorption relative to those slow excursions and could decay carbohydrates on board faster than reality once carbohydrates are announced. Dependencies: these become assessable only after the carbohydrate logging observation produces a real carbohydrates-on-board series; no change is supportable now.

Local hours 00:00 and 01:00 show the worst low burden of the period at 11.4 and 18.5 percent below range, which superficially suggests this rate is too high. The evidence separates against that: the low band self-resolves to 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL by local 02:00 and 03:00 while this same segment remains in force until 05:00, and zero temporary basals enacted overnight on 08-10, 08-16 and 08-17 did not prevent lows, which is only possible when the driver is insulin already delivered. Late-evening correction windows on 08-12 and 08-17 show falls of 56 to 68 mg/dL over four hours from doses of 0.05 to 0.15 units, confirming a carry-over tail under a 10-hour DIA. Uncertainty: rescue carbohydrate is unlogged, so the 02:00 recovery may be treatment-driven. Dependency: this cannot be evaluated until the insulin-on-board ceiling change and the quiet-evening comparison have been observed, and it must never move at the same time as DIA.

Local 05:00 and 06:00 are among the most stable hours of the entire period, with means of 104.2 and 99.5 mg/dL, above-range values of 0.0 percent and below-range values of 4.8 and 2.5 percent. There is no signal in either direction. Uncertainty: none material for this segment. Dependency: none; this segment is not implicated in any observed pattern.

Despite being the highest rate of the day, this segment produces the flattest results in the dataset: local 06:00 and 07:00 both average 99.5 mg/dL with 0.0 percent above range and only 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range, and local 08:00 shows 98.2 percent in range with zero below range. The rise that begins at local 09:00 and 10:00 falls partly inside this segment but cannot be attributed to it, because dawn effect and unlogged breakfast remain unseparated. Uncertainty: the single 42 mg/dL reading at 08-21 06:19 UTC preceded a sensor change by about three hours and is probably an end-of-life artefact rather than a true low. Dependency: separation requires carbohydrate recording, which is proposed as an observation step.

Local 10:00 shows 20.2 percent above range with a mean of 148.0 mg/dL, and the following hours climb further, which could suggest an insufficient rate. The evidence does not separate this from unannounced eating: carbohydrate entries are zero for the whole period, the loop responded with large temporary basals of 2.32 to 4.0 units per hour in this window, and rebound highs after unlogged rescue carbohydrate contribute to the same hours, as shown by 71 to 225 mg/dL within one hour on 08-12. Increasing this rate would also add delivery upstream of the local 19:00 low band at 15.3 percent below range. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: blocked pending seven days of carbohydrate recording and exclusion of the site and occlusion confounders.

Local 16:00 is the worst high hour at 32.1 percent above range with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 0.0 percent below range, while this is simultaneously the lowest basal rate of the day. Raising it is nonetheless not supported, because the hour is followed directly by local 18:00 and 19:00 at 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range, so added delivery here would feed the worst evening low band. The high itself is better explained by late detection of unannounced intake plus the two 180-minute raised temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18 that suppressed microbolusing, and by the 08-19 occlusion. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: this segment must not be touched before the eating-announcement observation and the mechanical checks are complete.

Local 18:00 shows 7.7 percent below range and contains severe readings of 42 to 51 mg/dL on 08-13. A reduction is a plausible response but is not yet supported, because each low cluster follows a high-glucose correction by two to five hours, for example the 08-14 correction at 234 mg/dL falling to 56 within 120 minutes, which identifies the tail of the afternoon response rather than this rate as the driver. Uncertainty: unlogged rescue carbohydrate and the concurrent GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 both affect this window. Dependency: reassess only after the insulin-on-board ceiling change has been observed, since that change targets the same mechanism.

Local 19:00 is the second-worst low hour at 15.3 percent below range with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL and contains the 41 to 48 mg/dL cluster on 08-14. This segment is the strongest basal-reduction candidate in the profile, but the same discriminator applies as at 18:00: the lows arrive as the tail of afternoon corrections rather than during steady-state fasting, and the hour also shows 4.3 percent above range with a maximum of 216 mg/dL, so the distribution is wide rather than uniformly low. Uncertainty: medium to high. Dependency: must be evaluated after, not with, the insulin-on-board ceiling change, and never together with DIA or the dynamic sensitivity factor.

No carbohydrates were entered during the 14-day period, so this segment was never exercised and cannot be validated or falsified. It appears only inside loop reason strings as an input to the dynamic sensitivity arithmetic. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate recording produces at least one entered meal in this window with six-hour follow-through.

Zero carbohydrate entries exist for the whole period, so no carbohydrate-to-outcome pair covers this window and no change can be supported. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked pending the seven-day carbohydrate recording observation.

This window covers the consistent local 09:00 and 10:00 rise to means of 132.9 and 148.0 mg/dL, but with zero carbohydrate entries that rise cannot be attributed to a carb ratio rather than to dawn effect or to unannounced intake. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: this is the window with the lowest hypoglycaemia risk, at 0.0 and 1.2 percent below range, so it is the safest place to begin carbohydrate recording, and only that observation can unblock this segment.

This is the strongest carb ratio of the day and it covers both the worst high hour at local 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and the worst evening low hours at 18:00 and 19:00. That combination makes it interesting, but with zero carbohydrate entries it has never been applied to a real meal and any change would be speculative. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked pending carbohydrate recording, and any future change here must be separated from the evening basal segments and from the insulin-on-board ceiling change.

No carbohydrates were entered in this or any other window during the period, so this segment cannot be assessed. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked pending the carbohydrate recording observation; note that any future change here would act upstream of the local 23:00 to 03:00 low band and must therefore be introduced cautiously and alone.

This is a deliberate single flat segment, consistent with the profile-switch label that references a flat ISF and with dynamic sensitivity being enabled. The value is overwritten every cycle: observed effective sensitivity spans 124.0 mg/dL per unit at 69.8 mg/dL down to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL, crossing 56 near 150 to 170 mg/dL. Editing this number therefore acts as a scaling input to the dynamic calculation rather than as a direct sensitivity change, and it cannot be separated from the dynamic adjustment factor. It also cannot be back-calculated from the correction windows, because those doses of 0.05 to 0.35 units were delivered against concurrent insulin on board of 1 to 6 units, so the observed falls measure the stack rather than the dose. Uncertainty: medium to high, and additionally scaled by the unresolved total daily dose. Dependency: this parameter and the dynamic adjustment factor act on the same quantity and must never move together; the factor is the more direct lever and is proposed for later consideration instead.

This target covers the worst low band of the period at local 01:00 with 18.5 percent below range, so raising it is superficially attractive. It is not supported, because the effective targets actually used by the loop span 80 to 116 mg/dL while only six temporary targets exist, all at or above profile target, and both Autosens target flags are false. The spread therefore originates in branch logic outside the reviewed inventory, and a profile target edit would have unpredictable effect. The low band is also better explained by an insulin tail than by the target, since it self-resolves by local 04:00 under the same target. Uncertainty: high, because the target-setting mechanism is not represented in the decision inventory. Dependency: reassess only after the insulin-on-board ceiling change and the quiet-evening comparison.

This daytime target covers both the afternoon high band peaking at 32.1 percent above range at local 16:00 and the evening low band at 15.3 percent below range at local 19:00, so no single direction of change is supported by the data. As with the other targets, sampled effective targets of 80 to 116 mg/dL show that the operative value is set by branch logic rather than directly by this segment. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: any target work must follow resolution of the sensitivity and announcement questions.

This one-hour segment covers local 23:00, which shows 10.1 percent below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL as part of the descent from 22:00 into the 01:00 nadir. It behaves identically to the 00:00 target segment and is subject to the same objection: the operative target is set by branch logic showing values from 80 to 116 mg/dL, and the descent is driven by decaying insulin rather than by target selection. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: evaluate together with the 00:00 target only after the insulin tail question is resolved, and not simultaneously with any basal or DIA change.

At 10 hours this is roughly double common settings and it is a confirmed co-driver of the overnight pattern, since it converts afternoon and evening dosing into a tail that coincides exactly with the local 22:00 to 01:00 decline from 127.6 to 90.6 mg/dL and the 18.5 percent below-range hour. Despite that, a change is withheld for three reasons. First, DIA is not the trigger for the large doses, which come from the high-glucose sensitivity amplification and the branch boosts. Second, shortening DIA reduces reported insulin on board and would make the loop dose more aggressively against a background already showing 5.1 percent below range and readings of 41 to 48 mg/dL. Third, it interacts directly with the proposed insulin-on-board ceiling change and must not move at the same time. Uncertainty: medium; no insulin activity or decay validation data exist in the package. Dependency: this is the designated next profile candidate after the quiet-evening verification described in the profile recommendation.

Both components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. With zero carbohydrate entries across 14 days, the unannounced-meal path is the only mechanism that responds to eating, and achieving 86.0 percent time in range with a mean of 121.6 mg/dL under those conditions is only possible because both are enabled. Disabling either would convert the afternoon burden of 20 to 32 percent above range at local 10:00 and 14:00 to 17:00 into a much larger problem. Evidence of active operation appears throughout the loop reason strings as unannounced-meal predictions and boosts. Uncertainty: low for this group. Dependency: this group is the enabler of the pattern but is not the driver; the drivers are the sensitivity amplification and the absent insulin-on-board ceiling, which are addressed separately.

All five components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. The group is internally consistent rather than contradictory: the always-on setting supersedes the two carbohydrate-linked settings, which are therefore inert and must not be read as restricting dosing around meals, and both are additionally inert because carbohydrate on board was zero throughout. The temporary-target setting was also effectively inert because all six temporary targets in the period were above profile target, at 135 mg/dL on five occasions and 108 on one, so with the high-temporary-target setting false, microbolusing was suppressed in every one of those windows. That suppression contributed to the 08-18 peak of 290 mg/dL and 15.3 percent above range, but given the dominant low burden of 5.1 percent below range with readings of 41 to 48 mg/dL, this is a defensible protective trade-off and loosening it would push against the primary safety signal. rationale: All three components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. The carbohydrate-linked 15-minute limit is inert because carbohydrate on board was zero throughout, leaving the 20-minute unannounced-meal allowance as the only size lever, and the evidence indicates it does not bind. With profile basal between 0.5 and 0.8 units per hour, 20 minutes equals roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units, yet a 0.4 unit microbolus was delivered on 08-07 against a stated standard maximum of 0.2, and a 1.6 unit boost was recorded on 08-19 while insulin on board was already 4.73 units. Reducing the allowance therefore has uncertain and probably low leverage, which is why the insulin-on-board ceiling is proposed as the first brake instead. Uncertainty: the 08-19 status reports 1.6 units while the matching therapy window records 0.65 units at the same timestamp, which may reflect partial delivery, split dosing or differing field scope, so the magnitude of the override is not precisely established. A secondary observation is recorded without a change: the unannounced-meal allowance of 20 minutes exceeds the carbohydrate-linked allowance of 15 minutes, granting the least-informed mode the larger allowance. Dependency: revisit only if the insulin-on-board ceiling change fails to reduce peak stacking, and never at the same time as that change.

Both components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible and a targeted change is used instead. Only the insulin-on-board component is proposed for change. Evidence: peaks of 4.73 units on 08-19 and 5.935 units on 08-21 reach just 24 percent of the 25 unit ceiling, so it has never engaged, while 5.935 units equals about 37 percent of the entire 16.2 unit scheduled daily basal; three sampled statuses on 08-11, 08-16 and 08-20 show 120-minute zero-basal suspends with predicted minimum guard values of minus 4, minus 59 and plus 28 mg/dL, demonstrating that delivered insulin regularly exceeds what remaining basal can offset, which links directly to 15.3 percent below range at local 19:00 and 18.5 percent at local 01:00. A candidate of 8 units sits above every observed peak in the sampled data yet well below a full day of insulin under either total-daily-dose interpretation, so it introduces a genuine tail ceiling without altering normal operation. The maximum basal component is deliberately left unchanged because it is inert: the binding ceiling comes from the safety multipliers, confirmed on 08-14 where an adjusted required rate of 5.9 was capped to a maximum safe basal of 4 units per hour, so 12 units per hour never engages and lowering it would change nothing until it fell below about 4. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 statuses are sampled, so true peak insulin on board may be higher than 5.935 units and the ceiling may engage more often than expected; total daily dose composition is unresolved between 19.7 and about 36 units per day, which affects the appropriate magnitude. Dependency: this must be the only insulin-delivery parameter changed in the first step, and must not be combined with the dynamic sensitivity factor, the flat ISF or DIA.

All five components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. The configuration is internally correct: Autosens disabled with dynamic sensitivity enabled is the coherent pairing, and both Autosens target flags being false is consistent with that. Sampled sensitivity ratios of 1, 0.98, 0.94, 0.92, 0.91, 0.88 and 0.79 are treated as neutral or dynamically derived current adjustments and are explicitly not used as evidence about whether Autosens is enabled. The adjustment factor of 70 percent is nonetheless the leading proximate driver of the observed pattern: against a flat profile value of 56 mg/dL per unit, effective sensitivity runs from 124.0 at 69.8 mg/dL to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL, crossing the profile value near 150 to 170 mg/dL, so dosing is roughly half strength in the low range and roughly double strength in the high range where every observed crash sequence began, compounding with branch boosts and a 3-minute interval. A change is withheld at this step only because the sequencing rule permits one brake at a time, and the insulin-on-board ceiling is the safer first move since it alters nothing in normal operation. Uncertainty: the appropriate magnitude is uncertain while total daily dose composition remains unresolved, since that quantity scales the dynamic calculation directly. Dependency: this factor and the flat ISF act on the same quantity and must never move together; reconsider this factor only after at least 14 days of observation following the insulin-on-board ceiling change.

Both components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. Both settings act only when carbohydrate on board exceeds zero, and carbohydrate on board was zero in every sampled loop status across the entire 14-day period with zero carbohydrate entries recorded, so neither setting was ever exercised and neither can have contributed to any observed pattern. No absorption duration has been inferred from any aggregate value, and the average extended carbohydrate duration field is null. Uncertainty: none regarding the current period, since the settings are demonstrably inert; complete regarding future behaviour, since no meal-linked evidence exists. Dependency: if carbohydrate recording begins as proposed, this group becomes live for the first time and would then need review alongside the 10-hour DIA, because a seven-hour absorption tail and a ten-hour insulin tail would overlap; that review is not possible until at least one carbohydrate entry with six-hour follow-through exists.

Evidence: local hours 00:00-03:00 average 91-105 mg/dL but carry 10.1-18.5 percent below range, the highest overnight low burden in the dataset. Uncertainty: the descent begins before midnight (128 at 22:00, 106 at 23:00 local) and negative IOB appears at 01:11 local, so this is more consistent with a carry-over insulin tail from evening dosing than with an excessive basal rate in this segment. Dependencies: resolution requires the automation overshoot to be reduced first and depends on the unverified 10-hour DIA with no declared insulin peak time. Reducing an already low overnight rate would not address the upstream cause.

suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
rationale: Evidence: this group governs essentially all dosing, because the unannounced-meal path is the only active one. The 20-minute ceiling sets the base that the fork boost multiplies: at 0.7 U/h basal the nominal cap is about 0.23 U and standardMaxBolus showed 0.2 U, yet 0.4 U was delivered; on 08-19 at 16:55 local at 0.5 U/h basal the nominal cap of about 0.17 U became 1.6 U delivered with 4.73 U already on board. Overshoot is corroborated by IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U against 16.2 U/day profile basal, reactive 120-minute zero-basal periods with minimum guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL, and falls of 108-178 mg/dL after doses of only 0.05-0.65 U. Only max_uam_smb_basal_minutes is proposed for change, from 20 to 15 minutes. The 3-minute interval is held because CGM cadence is 5.0 minutes, making it non-binding, and no remaining-time text was used to infer it. The 15-minute with-carbohydrate ceiling is held because it is dormant with zero carbohydrate-on-board. Uncertainty: the boost formula is fork-specific and undocumented, so it is not certain that delivered size scales linearly with this base; GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 and the 08-19 occlusion are additional confounders. Dependencies: this must be the only change in its cycle and must precede any maximum IOB or profile basal change.

Evidence: maximum basal of 12 U/h is not the binding constraint, since a reason string shows the adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to a maximum safe basal of 4, equal to the maximum daily safety multiplier of 5.0 times the peak profile basal of 0.8 U/h; changing 12 alone would have no effect. Maximum IOB of 25 U has never bound against a peak observed IOB of 5.935 U and a 16.2 U/day profile basal, so it offers no practical protection, and this is recorded as an issue and as the second recommendation. Uncertainty: the peak observed IOB was reached in a state whose outcome falls outside the data window, so the appropriate ceiling cannot be fixed from this package alone. Dependencies: this group targets the same failure mode as the microbolus delivery change; per the rule against changing dependent parameters together it is held in this cycle and reassessed only after at least 10 days of observation following that change. Both components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: observed sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and many at 1.0 show live adjustment, and a ratio of 1.0 is a neutral current adjustment rather than a disabled mechanism; these values are one-sided and never exceed 1.0, so all observed aggression originates from the dynamic sensitivity curve and the boost logic rather than from this ratio. Uncertainty: the 70 percent factor is a two-sided lever anchored to profile ISF. Reducing it would soften dosing at 245-262 mg/dL, where variable_sens reached 27.8-37.9 mg/dL/U, but would simultaneously strengthen dosing at 84-98 mg/dL, where the current 108-144 mg/dL/U is protective in the hours carrying 10.1-18.5 percent time below range. Dependencies: the observed failure is detection timing, not sensitivity magnitude, since 10:00-17:00 local remains 20-32 percent above range despite aggressive high-glucose dosing; this group is coupled to profile ISF and must not move alongside the delivery change. All components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: both parameters act on carbohydrate absorption and decay, and carbohydrate-on-board is zero in every sampled status, with carb_entries zero, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries zero and average_extended_carb_duration_min null. They are therefore inert in current usage. Uncertainty: no telemetry can validate or invalidate either value; the 7-hour maximum absorption is long but there is nothing to compare it against, and no e-carb duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: both become immediately relevant if the meal-announcement observation is undertaken, which is sequenced last; until then change is unsupported in either direction rather than the data being treated as a defect. Both components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: this segment covers 00:00 to 05:00 local, where time below range is 11.4, 18.5, 10.1, 10.2 and 3.0 percent for hours 00 through 04, and hourly means are flat at 90.6 to 106.0 mg/dL with no downward drift. Uncertainty: a uniformly excessive basal would depress the whole segment rather than concentrate lows in its first three hours, and the clean 04:00 to 07:00 window under the same and higher basal rates argues against a basal excess. The 2026-08-20 21:04 UTC status showing insulin on board of 2.802 units with a zero temporary basal already running supports a decaying insulin tail instead. Dependencies: this cannot be separated from DIA of 10 hours, from evening correction dosing and from the boost logic until the sensitivity change is tested, so no change is supported now.

Evidence: local hours 05 and 06 show 95.2 and 97.5 percent time in range, 4.8 and 2.5 percent below range and zero percent above range, with stable means of 104.2 and 99.5 mg/dL. Uncertainty: none material; this is one of the best-controlled windows in the dataset. Dependencies: none that would justify change, and altering a well-performing segment would add noise to the planned sequential tests. No change is supported.

Evidence: local hours 06 through 09 show 98.7, 98.2, 91.1 and 78.6 percent time in range with 1.3, 0.0, 0.0 and 1.2 percent below range. The rise begins at 08:00 to 09:00 and reaches a mean of 148.0 by 10:00. Uncertainty: that rise is too steep and too meal-shaped to be attributed to dawn basal, and with zero carbohydrate entries an unannounced breakfast covered reactively by UAM is the more plausible explanation. Dependencies: separating dawn phenomenon from meal effect requires the morning carbohydrate logging recommended separately, so no change is supported until then.

Evidence: local hours 10 through 15 show elevated means of 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1 and 153.0 mg/dL with time above range from 7.5 to 26.3 percent. Uncertainty: this window is dominated by unannounced intake handled reactively by UAM, and the same window is upstream of the evening lows, so a basal increase would risk adding insulin that lands during the 18:00 and 19:00 hypoglycemia window. Dependencies: meal effect, microbolus sizing and target modulation are all unresolved contributors here, so the pattern must not be attributed to basal. No change is supported.

Evidence: this is the profile's lowest basal and it coincides with the day's worst hour, local 16:00 with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range, which is a genuine face-value mismatch. Uncertainty: the same window is immediately followed by the highest evening time below range, 7.7 percent at 18:00 and 15.3 percent at 19:00, and every documented crash originates here, with falls of 168 to 178 mg/dL from logged boluses of only 0.2 to 0.65 units. That indicates the total insulin arriving in this window is already sufficient or excessive and is mistimed rather than insufficient. Dependencies: raising this segment would conflict with the safety constraint against adding insulin upstream of the 18:00 to 20:00 window and would confound the planned sensitivity test. Reconsider only after the sensitivity change has been observed and if afternoon highs persist without evening lows.

Evidence: local hour 18 shows 7.7 percent below range and 11.9 percent above range with a mean of 124.2 mg/dL, a mixed picture rather than a consistent direction. Uncertainty: the lows in this hour are attributable to the afternoon overcorrection cascade rather than to basal, because the falls of 168 and 178 mg/dL cannot be produced by the logged boluses of 0.2 and 0.65 units. Dependencies: a basal reduction here would blunt the measurable effect of the planned sensitivity change and would leave the actual cause untreated. No change is supported.

Evidence: local hour 19 carries the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL and a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and it contains the sustained cluster of 48, 41 and 41 mg/dL on 2026-08-14. Uncertainty: those readings occurred roughly two to three hours after a 234 mg/dL peak that triggered a 4 U/h temporary basal request and boosted microbolus dosing, so the insulin causing them was delivered earlier and elsewhere, not by this basal segment. Dependencies: the correct lever is the high-glucose aggressiveness addressed in the sensitivity recommendation, and changing basal here would mask that test. Revisit if the evening lows persist unchanged after the sensitivity observation period.

Evidence: zero carbohydrates were logged in 14 days, carb_treatment_entries is empty, and carbohydrate-on-board was zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so this ratio never influenced a bolus. The only related observation is that the loop reports 13.3 g/U in the overnight window against the profile 13.0 g/U across three samples, a difference of about 2 percent. Uncertainty: that small offset is not evidence of a wrong value and may reflect rounding or a percentage applied by the running build. Dependencies: verification requires announced carbohydrates, which the morning logging recommendation would begin to provide. No change is supported.

Evidence: the loop reads this value correctly, reporting 11.1 g/U in the corresponding local hours, but with zero carbohydrate entries it has never been exercised in a meal bolus. No change is supported.

Evidence: this segment covers the morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between 08:00 and 10:00 local, but that rise was handled entirely by UAM with no carbohydrate entry, so the ratio played no part in it. No change is supported until that data exists.

Evidence: the flat 56 mg/dL/U is a base value that dynamic sensitivity scales into an effective range of 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as strong as profile above 200 mg/dL and roughly half as strong below 100 mg/dL. The most aggressive values coincide with the crashes, including sensitivity of 37.9 mg/dL/U with insulinReq of 1.98 units on 2026-08-19 and 27.8 mg/dL/U with insulinReq of 2.12 units on 2026-08-21. Uncertainty: profile ISF and the 70 percent dynamic factor multiply into the same effective number and cannot be separated from this data, and weakening the base value would also weaken the already-mild low-glucose behavior where effective sensitivity is 108 to 124 mg/dL/U. Dependencies: this row is explicitly held in reserve as the fallback lever behind the dynamic factor change, and changing both would make the result uninterpretable. Revisit only if the sensitivity factor reduction proves insufficient after at least 10 days.

Evidence: this target covers 00:00 to 08:00 local, where time below range is elevated in hours 00 to 03 at 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent but excellent in hours 04 to 07. Uncertainty: the loop is already applying its own target modulation, with observed values from 80 to 116 mg/dL against the three declared profile targets, through a mechanism absent from the supplied settings. Raising the profile target would interact unpredictably with that modulation and would also mask, rather than resolve, the insulin-tail explanation for the early-overnight lows. Dependencies: the target modulation conflict must be understood before any profile target change is meaningful. No change is supported.

Evidence: this target covers 08:00 to 23:00 local, the window containing both the daytime highs and the evening lows. Loop statuses in these hours report effective targets of 80, 82, 87, 90, 99, 104, 108 and 116 mg/dL, so the declared 100 mg/dL is frequently not the value in use. Uncertainty: the declared autosens_lowers_target is false, yet targets fall to 80 mg/dL during high and rising glucose, which is a direct conflict between declared settings and observed behavior that this package cannot resolve. Dependencies: adjusting the profile target while an undocumented modulation is active would produce an uninterpretable result. No change is supported, and the conflict is reported instead.

Evidence: local hour 23 shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with 88.7 percent in range, 10.1 percent below range and 1.2 percent above range, at the start of the overnight hypoglycemia cluster. Uncertainty: as with the other target rows, the lows here are better explained by the decaying insulin tail from evening dosing than by the target value, and the loop applies its own modulation regardless. Dependencies: tied to the same unresolved target-modulation mechanism and to the DIA question. No change is supported.

Evidence: a 10-hour DIA is mechanistically consistent with the repeated late declines in the therapy response windows, including minus 68 mg/dL at 240 minutes from a 0.05-unit bolus and minus 67 and minus 66 mg/dL at 240 and 360 minutes from a 0.2-unit bolus, and with the recurrent negative insulin on board of minus 0.481, minus 0.197 and minus 0.159 units after prolonged zero temporary basals. Uncertainty: DIA is confounded with the steepened dynamic sensitivity, with microbolus stacking at a 3-minute interval and with the insulin peak time, which is not supplied in the package, and no isolated DIA test exists in the data. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change insulin-on-board accounting across every other lever simultaneously and must not be combined with the planned sensitivity test. No change is supported now.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. With zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrate-on-board of zero in all 24 sampled statuses, UAM is the only mechanism covering meals, and it delivers 86.0 percent time in range without any carbohydrate announcement. UAM is not duplicating carbohydrate-on-board counting here because carbohydrate-on-board is genuinely zero throughout. Uncertainty: the aggressiveness of the UAM response is a concern, but that is governed by the boost logic, the sensitivity factor and the microbolus caps, not by these two on-off switches. Dependencies: disabling either would remove all meal coverage and would worsen the daytime highs without addressing the overcorrection cause. No change is supported.

Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. The group is internally coherent: smb_always_enabled true makes the two carbohydrate-conditional flags inert in the current data, and smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false means microboluses are suppressed while a high temporary target runs, which occurred during the 180-minute 135 mg/dL targets on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18. Uncertainty: 2026-08-18 shows both the highest time below range at 12.8 percent and 15.3 percent above range, so that suppression window contributes to variability, but it appears to be deliberate hypoglycemia-avoidance behavior rather than a misconfiguration. current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: all three components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. The 3-minute interval is taken from the configured setting and not from any waiting message, and it is a standard value. The caps compute to 0.18 to 0.20 units and 0.23 to 0.27 units at the current basal rates, and the loop reports exactly these as standardMaxBolus. Uncertainty: delivery demonstrably exceeds them, with standardMaxBolus 0.2 followed by a 0.4-unit microbolus on 2026-08-07, Increased SMB as percentage on 2026-08-18 and a 1.6-unit microbolus on 2026-08-19, driven by boost parameters that are not present in the supplied settings. Reducing these caps therefore has an unpredictable effect and could produce no benefit while consuming an observation cycle. Dependencies: this lever acts on the same effective dose as profile ISF and the dynamic sensitivity factor and must not be changed alongside either. It is held as the third-line option behind max IOB and the sensitivity factor.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable and a supported change exists. max_iob of 25 units stands against roughly 19.7 units of bolus and microbolus insulin per day and a peak observed insulin on board of 5.935 units on 2026-08-21, so the ceiling is one to two days of insulin and is never approached. It therefore provides no practical backstop against the large high-glucose requests observed, insulinReq 1.98 units on 2026-08-19 and 2.12 units on 2026-08-21. A value of 10 units retains substantial headroom above every observed value while restoring a meaningful limit. max_basal is deliberately left at 12 U/h because it is not the binding constraint: the logs show adj. req. rate 5.9 to maxSafeBasal 4, so the real 4.0 to 4.2 U/h ceiling comes from max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier of 6, which lie outside this group. Uncertainty: the appropriate max IOB depends on the user's usual peak insulin on board across a longer period than the 24 sampled statuses, so the candidate value must be checked against the user's own records before use. Dependencies: this is the only lever that confounds no other test, which is why it is sequenced first and alone.

Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. Effective sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U around the flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U and becomes roughly twice as strong as profile above 200 mg/dL. The strongest values coincide precisely with the overcorrection events: 37.9 mg/dL/U with 4.73 units on board before the fall from 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes on 2026-08-19, and 27.8 mg/dL/U with 5.935 units on board on 2026-08-21. Six of 24 therapy response windows fall below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours. Reducing the factor from 70 to 60 percent is a single, reversible step that blunts high-glucose aggressiveness while leaving the profile ISF anchor and the mild low-glucose behavior intact. Uncertainty: the observed target modulation from 80 to 116 mg/dL contradicts the declared autosens target flags and originates in boost logic absent from the supplied settings, so part of the aggressiveness may not respond to this factor; sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.0 are read as neutral or mild current adjustments, not as a disabled function. Dependencies: this must not be changed together with profile ISF or the microbolus caps, which act on the same effective dose, and it should follow the completed max IOB observation period.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable. Both settings are functionally inert in this dataset because carbohydrate-on-board was zero in every sampled loop status and no carbohydrate entry exists, so neither value has ever been exercised. min_5m_carbimpact of 8 is the standard value and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 is only slightly above the usual 6. Uncertainty: the package contains no evidence at all about either value, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate average, since average_extended_carb_duration_min is null. Dependencies: changing an untested parameter would add noise to the sequential validation of the max IOB and sensitivity changes. These become testable only after the recommended morning carbohydrate logging produces real carbohydrate-on-board. No change is supported.

Hours 00 and 01 local average 93.3 and 90.6 mg/dL with time below range of 11.4 and 18.5 percent, which superficially suggests basal excess. However three overnight loop samples show negative or near-zero insulin-on-board (-0.481, -0.197 and 0.083 U), meaning the loop had already withheld basal before the lows, which points to a residual tail from earlier dosing rather than to the scheduled overnight rate. Uncertainty is high because only three overnight statuses are available out of 6214. Dependency: this cannot be separated from the 10-hour duration of insulin action or from the maximum insulin-on-board change, and must not be altered in the same step.

Hour 05 local averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range, zero time above range and 4.8 percent below range. This is one of the best-controlled hours in the dataset and there is no evidence supporting a change. Uncertainty is low for this segment. Dependency: none that would justify altering it.

Hours 06 to 08 local average 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with time in range of 97.5, 98.7 and 98.2 percent and time below range of 2.5, 1.3 and 0.0 percent. The fasting-like morning window is well matched and shows no dawn phenomenon, so the step up to 0.8 U/h appears supported by outcome. Uncertainty is low. Dependency: the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 08-21 occurred two hours before a sensor change and is treated as a probable artifact rather than as evidence against this segment.

Hours 10 to 15 local show rising averages from 148.0 to 153.0 mg/dL with time above range of 7.5 to 26.3 percent, which could suggest insufficient basal. Dependency: this is an independent safety limit and must be implemented alone, before any basal, duration or sensitivity work, so its effect can be attributed.

Dynamic sensitivity is the sole adaptive path and produces effective sensitivity from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as aggressive as the static 56 mg/dL/U at high glucose and roughly twice as conservative at low glucose, which plausibly links the afternoon highs to the early-evening lows. Change is withheld because two explanations are unseparated: dynamic sensitivity being too aggressive at high glucose, versus dynamic sensitivity compensating for a basal shape whose minimum falls at the hyperglycemia peak and for entirely absent carbohydrate announcement. The adjustment factor is a single global knob that cannot moderate the high-glucose end without further weakening the already-slow low-glucose end. Uncertainty is medium-high because the fork formula variant is not supplied. Dependency: revisit only after the maximum insulin-on-board change is verified and after the basal-versus-duration question is resolved; this is the last parameter in the safe order.

A ceiling of 8 U sits above every observed peak, so routine dosing is unaffected while an actual brake on extreme accumulation is introduced. Dependencies: coupled to the flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, at most one of the two may move, and both must wait until the maximum insulin on board change is evaluated.
