First, with dynamic sensitivity enabled and autosens disabled the loop never used 56 for its own dosing, since every sampled status quotes an effective sensitivity between 27.8 and 124 mg/dL/U, so the profile value governs the bolus calculator rather than closed-loop correction. Second, 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U at 0.42 U per entry, with basal appearing separately as temp basal rate events, indicates the figure is bolus and SMB only and implies roughly 36 U per day with the 16.2 U scheduled basal, making 56 defensible. Uncertainty: the insulin total is not explicitly labelled, so this inference is held at medium confidence. Dependencies: the correction lever belongs on the dynamic ISF adjustment factor instead, and these two must never be changed together.

Evidence: a higher overnight target would be a plausible response to 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range in local hours 22:00 to 01:00, but sampled statuses report working targets of 80, 84, 86 and 87 mg/dL while the profile states 90 and both autosens target-adjustment switches are false, so an unidentified mechanism is already overriding the profile value and editing the profile number may not produce the intended effect. Uncertainty: high, and part of this below-range band may be sensor artefact. Dependencies: blocked pending clarification of the target override.

Evidence: the window covered by this target contains both the best block of the day, 04:00 to 09:00 local flat and in range, and the worst above-range block, 10:00 to 17:00, so no single target change would serve both. Lowering it would add risk to the 18:00 to 19:00 crash while raising it would worsen the afternoon peak. Uncertainty: the same unexplained working-target override applies, since values of 80 and 87 were observed against a profile value of 100. Dependencies: blocked pending clarification of the override.

Evidence: this segment begins the highest below-range band of the day and is a genuine future candidate, but it is kept because the effective working target is already lower than the profile value through an unidentified mechanism and no inventory setting in the package explains it. Uncertainty: high, and the artefact question for the 00:00 to 03:00 lows is unresolved. Dependencies: clarification of the target override, and it must not be changed alongside any basal or automation change.

Evidence: DIA 10 hours is long, but shortening it is unsupported and would likely be harmful, because therapy response windows repeatedly show real glucose change still occurring at 240 and 360 minutes, for example 08-19 with minus 161 mg/dL at 240 minutes and minus 176 at 360, and 08-17 with minus 68 and minus 50. A shorter DIA would under-report insulin on board and permit more stacking, the opposite of what the observed pattern needs. Uncertainty: these tails are confounded by concurrent temp basal delivery, so DIA cannot be isolated from automation dosing. Dependencies: DIA amplifies but does not cause the pattern, so the limits and the sensitivity factor are the operative levers.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted and the decision is keep. With 0 carb entries and COB reported as 0 throughout, UAM is the only mechanism delivering meal-responsive insulin, and time in range of 86.0 percent with a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent was achieved without any carbohydrate announcement. Disabling either switch would remove the response to the 09:00 to 16:00 rise and would very likely worsen the 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 without a compensating meal-announcement strategy. Uncertainty: low for this decision. Dependencies: the strength of the UAM response, not its existence, is the issue, and that is addressed through the sensitivity factor.

Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. smb_always_enabled true functionally overrides the two COB-linked switches, which are inert while no carbohydrates are logged, an internal inconsistency but not a safety concern today. The live interaction is smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false combined with repeated 135 mg/dL temporary targets, twice for 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18, which suppresses SMB during the highest above-range hours. Enabling it is explicitly not recommended, because it would inject SMB into the windows the user appears to be using as protection against the documented level-2 clusters, and on 08-18 the 290 mg/dL peak preceded the temporary target rather than resulting from it. Uncertainty: whether the temporary targets are a deliberate crash workaround is not confirmed in the package. Dependencies: re-evaluate after the sensitivity change and after carbohydrate logging begins.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: all three components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. An earlier working view treated this group as a change candidate and it is downgraded to keep, because these caps do not control actual delivery: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 against a 0.5 to 0.8 U/h basal implies a ceiling near 0.17 to 0.27 U, yet observed SMB sizes were 0.4 U where standardMaxBolus was 0.2 U and 1.6 U under a UAM High Boost, so the build-specific boost exceeds the configured cap. Tightening a cap that is already bypassed would give a false sense of control while consuming an observation window. The 3-minute interval also never throttles anything against a 5-minute CGM cadence. Uncertainty: the boost multipliers are not exposed in the package. Dependencies: reconsider only if the sensitivity factor change fails to reduce the evening below-range band, and only as a single isolated change.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted and change is used with supported old and new values. Only the insulin-on-board component changes. max_basal_u_per_hour stays at 12 U/h because it is inert, since the operative ceiling is about 4 U/h from the default multipliers, confirmed by the 08-14 log line reducing a required 5.9 U/h to maxSafeBasal 4, so editing it would change nothing observable. max_iob_units drops from 25 U to 8 U because 25 U is 70 to 125 percent of an estimated 36 U total daily dose and never engaged in 14 days, while the observed working maximum was 5.935 U on 08-21 at glucose 245.7 with a requested 2.12 U and a 4 U/h rate, an episode whose outcome is unobserved because the data window ends there. A value of 8 U leaves clear headroom above observed use while ending an effectively unbounded allowance. Stated honestly, because this limit never bound it would not by itself have prevented the 08-13 or 08-14 clusters, where insulin on board was only about 1.4 to 1.6 U, so it is a tail-risk guardrail rather than the fix for the observed pattern. Uncertainty: the total daily dose estimate rests on an unlabelled field and should be confirmed before applying. Dependencies: apply in its own observation window, never together with the sensitivity factor change.

Evidence: all five components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. Only the adjustment factor changes, from 70 to 60 percent; the four switches stay as they are because the configuration is internally consistent, with autosens and dynamic sensitivity correctly not stacked and both target-adjustment switches off. The reported sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.0 are the current neutral to resistance-direction output of the dynamic model and are not evidence about the autosens switch, so they do not justify enabling autosens. The factor is reduced because it produces the four-fold sensitivity spread that drives the observed pattern, from 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose down to 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose 262 and 245.7 with insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.94 U, roughly twice as aggressive as the profile ISF of 56 precisely in the state preceding both level-2 clusters. Trade-off stated plainly: this single global factor acts in opposite directions on the two problems, so it will also weaken correction in the 10:00 to 17:00 block where time above range reaches 32.1 percent, and the balance between 5.1 percent below range and 8.9 percent above range is a care-team judgement. Uncertainty: medium, because the build applies undocumented UAM Boost and dosing-sensitivity layers on top of this factor, so the realised effect may be smaller or larger than the factor change implies. Dependencies: this is the primary change and must run alone, never combined with the insulin-on-board limit, any basal segment, or profile ISF.

Evidence: both components have non-null values, so verify is not permitted. Both parameters act only on the COB and carbohydrate-absorption path, which was completely unexercised, with 0 carb entries, 0.0 g total, no extended carb entries and COB reported as 0 in all 24 sampled statuses, so no observation in this dataset can support or refute either value, and min_5m_carbimpact of 8 is a conventional setting. One forward-looking caution rather than a change: both become active the moment carbohydrate entry begins, and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 combined with DIA 10 hours could sustain dosing into the 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 01:00 windows that already carry 7.7 to 18.5 percent below range. Uncertainty: complete, since the path has never run. Dependencies: revisit only after carbohydrate logging has produced real absorption curves.

Evidence: the fasting curve across this segment rises rather than falls, with local means of 93.3 at 00:00, 90.6 at 01:00, 101.9 at 02:00 and 104.7 at 03:00, and time in range of 88.6, 81.5, 89.9 and 89.2 percent. Uncertainty: time below range in this block is elevated at 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, but a rising mean with a heavy left tail points to carry-over insulin on board rather than basal excess. Dependencies: the same lows are explained by the late-tail mechanism targeted by the automation change, so this segment must not be altered in the same window or the two effects become inseparable.

Evidence: the 05:00 and 06:00 local hours show means of 104.2 and 99.5 mg/dL with time in range of 95.2 and 97.5 percent and time above range of 0.0 percent. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment; the single 42 mg/dL reading on 2026-08-21 at 07:19 local is an isolated outlier within an otherwise strong block. Dependencies: none that would justify change; this segment is part of the best-performing period of the day.

Evidence: the 06:00 to 09:00 local block covered by this segment shows means of 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL with time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2 and 91.1 percent and time below range of 2.5, 1.3, 0.0 and 0.0 percent. Uncertainty: the rise toward 10:00 local reaching 148.0 mg/dL begins inside this segment, but with zero carb entries a morning meal is the more plausible driver than basal. Dependencies: separating meal from basal here requires the carbohydrate logging step, so no change is supported yet.

Evidence: the 10:00 to 16:00 local block covered by this segment carries substantial time above range of 20.2, 7.5, 14.0, 16.6, 26.3 and 23.6 percent. Uncertainty: this is the core of the unannounced-meal band, and temporary targets of 135 mg/dL lasting 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18 suppressed microboluses inside it, so the elevation cannot be attributed to basal. Dependencies: raising basal here would add insulin ahead of the 18:00-19:00 low window where time below range reaches 15.3 percent, which the 5.1 percent overall time below range does not permit.

Evidence: this lowest basal segment coincides with the highest local hour of 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range, which makes it the strongest profile candidate in the dataset. Uncertainty: the evidence does not separate a low basal from unannounced afternoon intake, since there are zero carb entries in 14 days, and severe highs in this window on 08-15 and 08-18 coincide with a suppressive temporary target and a pump occlusion respectively. Dependencies: the 18:00-19:00 low window with 15.3 percent below range sits directly downstream of this segment, so any increase risks deepening the existing low pattern; this becomes a supported candidate only after carbohydrate logging separates the two explanations.

Evidence: the 18:00 local hour shows a mean of 124.2 mg/dL with 11.9 percent above range and 7.7 percent below range, a mixed rather than one-directional pattern. Uncertainty: the two level-2 lows on 08-13 and 08-14 fall at the edge of this segment, but both are the tail of afternoon excursions reaching 234 and 264 mg/dL rather than independent basal lows. Dependencies: attributing these lows to basal would contradict the late-tail mechanism supported by insulin on board of 4.73 to 5.94 U and the 10-hour DIA, so no change is made here.

Evidence: the 19:00 local hour has the highest single-hour time below range of the day at 15.3 percent with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL, which superficially suggests a basal reduction. Uncertainty: the mean is not low, and the pattern is driven by deep excursions following afternoon highs rather than by a sustained downward drift, which is the signature of accumulated insulin rather than basal excess. Dependencies: the automation change to the UAM microbolus base targets exactly this mechanism, and changing both together would make the result uninterpretable; this segment should be re-evaluated after that observation window.

Evidence: zero carb entries, zero grams of carbohydrate and zero extended carb entries across 14 days, with COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status, mean this segment was never exercised by real use. Uncertainty: the value appears in loop reason strings, which confirms the profile was active but validates nothing about its accuracy. Dependencies: assessment is blocked until carbohydrate logging begins; changing an untested value would introduce risk without evidence.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was announced in this or any window during the period, so no bolus-to-carb pairing exists. Uncertainty: reason strings echo carb ratio values of 10.5 to 13.3 by time of day, confirming profile activity only. Dependencies: blocked by the same zero-carb data gap that blocks all carb ratio segments; the carbohydrate logging step is the prerequisite.

Evidence: a clean morning rise from 99.5 at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 local is visible, but with zero carb entries no carbohydrate quantity is known, so no ratio can be derived from it. Uncertainty: the rise could be a meal, dawn effect or both, and the package does not separate them. Dependencies: requires announced carbohydrate with accurate timestamps before any assessment is possible.

Evidence: this segment covers the highest-elevation part of the day, with 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 and 22.6 percent at 17:00 local, but zero carbohydrate was announced so the ratio was never applied. Uncertainty: the elevation is real, yet attributing it to a carb ratio requires knowing the carbohydrate amount, which is absent. Dependencies: this is the specific segment that the recommended carbohydrate logging for the 12:00-17:00 meal would first make assessable.

Evidence: the 20:00 to 23:00 local hours show a modest rise from 117.0 to 127.6 mg/dL with low time above range of 4.2 to 7.2 percent, and no carbohydrate was announced. Uncertainty: any evening intake was covered reactively by automation, so the ratio itself is untested. Dependencies: blocked by the zero-carb data gap; no change supported.

Evidence: with autosens disabled and dynamic sensitivity enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor, the effective sensitivity actually used ranged from 124 mg/dL/U at low glucose with negative insulin on board to 27.8 mg/dL/U at 246 mg/dL with 5.94 U on board, so the profile value is largely nominal in practice. Uncertainty: correction response windows cannot yield an empirical value because labelled boluses of 0.05 to 0.35 U are accompanied by 4 to 6 hour changes ranging from -176 to +135 mg/dL, dominated by automated delivery and unannounced intake; the u200 dilute label also blocks any total-daily-dose-normalised cross-check. Dependencies: the effective lever is the dynamic ISF adjustment factor rather than this segment, and that is deliberately deferred to a separate later step, so changing this value now would be masked and would confound the automation observation.

Evidence: the overnight block shows a rising mean from 90.6 to 106.0 mg/dL with time in range of 81.5 to 95.8 percent, so the target is not producing a sustained downward drift. Uncertainty: loop statuses report target_bg values including 80 mg/dL that the profile does not contain and that logged temporary targets do not explain; per profile_context the profile remains authoritative, and this unresolved conflict lowers confidence in target-linked inference. Dependencies: raising the overnight target could mask the late-tail insulin mechanism rather than correct it, so the automation change should be observed first.

Evidence: the daytime block covered by this target contains both the highest elevation at 16:00 local and the highest single-hour time below range at 19:00 local, a bidirectional pattern that a single target change cannot address in one direction. Uncertainty: the same unexplained target_bg discrepancy applies, and temporary targets of 135 mg/dL were used on five occasions within this block, indicating the user already raises the target situationally. Dependencies: the microbolus and dynamic ISF mechanisms explain the variability better than the target does, and both are sequenced ahead of any target change.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with only 1.2 percent above range but 10.1 percent below range, so the low exposure begins as this segment starts. Uncertainty: this is the entry point of the overnight low window, which the evidence attributes to residual insulin from evening activity rather than to the target value itself. Dependencies: the same late-tail mechanism as the 00:00 target and the evening basal segments; changing the target concurrently with the automation change would confound both.

Evidence: a 10-hour DIA with free-peak insulin extends every boosted microbolus tail, and observed insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.94 U represents roughly 7 to 9 hours of profile basal in a single stack, with both low windows sitting 2 to 6 hours after the daily aggression peaks. Uncertainty: this is a timing association, not a measurement; no clean isolated bolus without subsequent delivery exists in the sample, so DIA cannot be measured directly from this package. Dependencies: DIA changes the insulin activity model globally and would alter the interpretation of every insulin-on-board figure used elsewhere in this analysis, so it must not move alongside the microbolus change; it is best reviewed with the care team only after the automation observation window.

Evidence: with zero carb entries and COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status, microboluses and UAM are the only meal coverage present, and the workflow still achieves 86.0 percent time in range. Uncertainty: UAM is central to the accumulation mechanism, but no duplicate carb-on-board counting is present, since UAM predictions never appear alongside a non-zero COB. Dependencies: disabling either switch would remove all meal coverage rather than reduce risk; the supported approach is to scale the microbolus base instead, which is handled under aaps.core.smb_delivery. Both components have non-null values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: the pairing of microboluses permitted with a temporary target but not with a high temporary target is protective and demonstrably active, since the 135 mg/dL temporary targets lasting 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18 suppressed microboluses inside the afternoon window. Uncertainty: smb_always_enabled true supersedes both smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false, so those two flags are currently inert and will remain inert once carbohydrate logging begins; this is a consistency note, not a defect. Dependencies: the group is coherent and no change is supported; the suppression it causes is itself a confounder for the afternoon pattern and must be accounted for when the carbohydrate logging results are reviewed. All components are non-null, so verify is not applicable.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
rationale: Evidence: reason strings confirm the basal-minutes setting sets the microbolus sizing base, with 0.7 U/h basal producing standardMaxBolus 0.2 and 0.8 U/h producing standardMaxBolus 0.3 at 20 minutes; boost logic then delivered 0.4 U against a 0.2 U base and, in a UAM High Boost case on 08-19, 1.6 U with 4.73 U already on board. Across the period, roughly 47 microbolus events per day averaged about 0.42 U, exceeding the reconstructed base. Reducing the UAM base from 20 to 15 basal-minutes aligns it with the existing non-UAM cap and proportionally scales boosted output. Uncertainty: the boost multipliers, including one value of 35.93 seen on 08-13, are not exposed as configurable items, so this reduces but does not bound the worst case; effect size cannot be predicted from the sampled data. Dependencies: only max_uam_smb_basal_minutes changes; smb_interval_minutes stays at 3 minutes and max_smb_basal_minutes stays at 15 minutes, and no profile row or dynamic ISF setting may change in the same observation window, otherwise the low-window response cannot be attributed.

suggested_value: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h; max_iob_units=a reachable backstop with clear headroom above the observed peak of 5.94 U, for example 8-10 U, to be confirmed with the care team
rationale: Evidence: peak observed insulin on board was 5.94 U against a 25 U limit, approximately 1.27 times the 14-day mean daily bolus insulin of 19.7 U, so the limit has never engaged and could not have limited any observed event, including the falls of -178 and -176 mg/dL. Uncertainty: this value also caps the calculated insulin requirement, so it is delivery-affecting rather than a pure backstop, and it must retain clear headroom above normal operation; the exact value is for the care team to set, and the u200 dilute label means unit magnitudes may not compare to standard assumptions. Dependencies: max_basal_u_per_hour is kept unchanged because it never binds, since the effective 4 U/h ceiling observed on 08-14 derives from the safety multiplier applied to the largest basal segment; this guardrail adjustment should be made in a separate step from the microbolus change. Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: the configuration is internally consistent, and the observed sensitivity_ratio values of 1.0, 0.98, 0.94, 0.92, 0.91, 0.88 and 0.79 are neutral to mildly resistant current adjustments rather than evidence of a disabled autosens. The 70 percent adjustment factor produced effective sensitivity from 124 down to 27.8 mg/dL/U, hardening most at high glucose with high insulin on board, which is the mechanism most closely associated with the two large falls. Uncertainty: the direction of a reduction is supported but the magnitude is not, because the sampled statuses do not quantify how much of each fall came from dynamic ISF versus boost logic versus temp basal. Dependencies: this setting acts on both microboluses and temp basals, making it broader and riskier than the microbolus base, so it is deliberately held at its current value and reserved as a separate later step after the aaps.core.smb_delivery observation window; changing both together would violate the rule against moving dependent settings simultaneously. All components are non-null, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: both values are functionally inert in this period because COB is 0 in every sampled loop status, there are zero carb entries and zero extended carb entries, and the 20 gram minimum carbohydrate requirement is never reached. Uncertainty: min_5m_carbimpact still participates in deviation classification that feeds unannounced-meal handling, but no evidence in the package separates its contribution from the boost logic; the sustained 11:00-17:00 plateau is suggestive of slow absorption but is equally explainable by repeated unannounced intake, and no duration is inferred from curve shape or from any aggregate average. Dependencies: these settings only become reviewable once carbohydrate logging produces real carb-on-board data, so they are held unchanged. Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: time below range at 00:00 local is 11.4 percent and at 01:00 local is 18.5 percent, which is the highest of any hour, but the 04:00 to 07:00 local window on the adjacent 0.6 and 0.7 U/h segments shows 95 to 99 percent time in range. Uncertainty: the overnight lows follow evening excursions reaching 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL and a 10-hour DIA keeps evening insulin active, so an insulin tail is at least as plausible as basal excess. Dependencies: cannot be separated from the SMB frequency and dynamic sensitivity changes proposed ahead of it, and the effective overnight target is uncertain because loop targets ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL. Withholding change until the night-stratification check is complete.

Evidence: the 05:00 local hour shows 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent time below range, and no time above range, and the 06:00 and 07:00 hours are similarly strong. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment; the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21 occurred on the day of a sensor change and is excluded from attribution. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; this segment is one of the best-performing parts of the profile.

Evidence: the 06:00 to 09:00 local hours show time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2, and 91.1 percent with time below range of 2.5 percent or less, indicating the dawn step is well matched. Uncertainty: the rise beginning at 08:00 local reaches 148.0 mg/dL by 10:00 with 20.2 percent time above range, but with zero carbohydrate entries this is most consistent with an unannounced morning meal rather than a dawn basal deficit. Dependencies: resolution requires the morning carbohydrate logging observation before any basal change here could be justified.

Evidence: hours 10:00 to 15:00 local average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1, and 153.0 mg/dL with time above range of 7.5 to 26.3 percent. Uncertainty: high. Loop statuses across this window report COB 0 with deviations of 2.3 to 7.1 and insulin requirements up to 2.59 units, the signature of unannounced intake rather than a fasting basal shortfall, and no fasting window exists in the data to test the segment. Dependencies: any upward change here would add insulin that remains active into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster under a 10-hour DIA, so it must wait until that cluster is resolved.

Evidence: the 16:00 local hour has the highest average of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent time above range and 0.0 percent time below range, and it carries the lowest basal rate in the profile, which superficially suggests underdosing. Uncertainty: high, and the earlier working hypothesis of a basal deficit here is explicitly retired. Two of the worst afternoons, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, had 180-minute temporary targets of 135 mg/dL that suppressed SMB entirely because smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, and all afternoon rises are unannounced. Dependencies: raising this segment would feed the 18:00 to 19:00 window where time below range is 7.7 and 15.3 percent with 41 and 42 mg/dL nadirs, so change is unsafe before the automation steps and carbohydrate logging are evaluated.

Evidence: the 18:00 local hour shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the 2026-08-13 level-2 episode falls in this hour. Uncertainty: high as to cause. That episode followed a 0.2 unit correction at 172 mg/dL roughly five hours earlier and a documented afternoon UAM sequence, so the insulin tail under a 10-hour DIA is the leading explanation rather than the basal rate itself. Dependencies: the max_iob, dynamic sensitivity, and SMB interval steps all reduce the same tail; changing basal at the same time would make attribution impossible.

Evidence: the 19:00 local hour has the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the basal schedule steps up into this hour, which appears counterintuitive. Uncertainty: high. The 2026-08-14 level-2 episode in this hour followed a 0.2 unit correction at 234 mg/dL plus a 1.1 unit bolus about two to three hours earlier, and the loop enacted 3.6 U/h at 19:40 local, so delivered insulin dominates the scheduled basal contribution here. Dependencies: this hour is the primary readout for the max_iob and dynamic sensitivity steps, so it must be observed unchanged while those are tested.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, and carb_treatment_entries is empty for the full 14 days, so this ratio never drove a meal bolus. Uncertainty: complete for meal dosing; the value is not validated, only untested. Dependencies: it still feeds the dynamic sensitivity computation, since carb ratio values appear in loop reason strings, so it is not inert, but any change would alter that computation without a single meal outcome to justify it. Change withheld until carbohydrate logging produces evidence.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist in the period, and the 04:00 to 08:00 local window shows 95.2 to 98.7 percent time in range with no meal signature. Uncertainty: complete; the ratio is untestable. Dependencies: the value appears in loop reason strings and therefore scales dynamic sensitivity, so changing it blindly would confound the sensitivity step that is already proposed. Keep.

Evidence: a consistent morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL exists between 08:00 and 10:00 local, but with zero carbohydrate entries no bolus was ever calculated from this ratio. Uncertainty: complete for validation purposes. Dependencies: this is the specific ratio that the proposed morning carbohydrate logging observation would first make testable, so change is deliberately deferred to after that observation rather than guessed now.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist, so this ratio has not been exercised for meal dosing. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: this ratio applies to the 16:00 to 20:00 local window that contains both the day's highest average glucose and, from 18:00, the day's worst hypoglycemia exposure; any change here would act on both problems simultaneously in opposite directions and cannot be evaluated. Keep.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist, despite a clear recurring evening rise reaching 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL between 20:00 and 23:00 local. Uncertainty: complete for validation. Dependencies: this window feeds directly into the 23:00 to 03:00 hypoglycemia cluster, so it is the least safe place to introduce additional meal insulin before the overnight cause is separated. Keep.

Evidence: dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and autosens is disabled, and observed effective sensitivity ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, so the flat 56 value is an anchor rather than the operative sensitivity. Uncertainty: the asymmetric dosing behavior is real and well evidenced, but it is produced by the scaling factor around this anchor, not by the anchor alone. Dependencies: changing the anchor and the dynamic factor together would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule and would make the result uninterpretable, so the factor is proposed as the single lever and the anchor is kept unchanged.

Evidence: overnight time below range is 11.4 percent at 00:00 and 18.5 percent at 01:00 local, which would normally support raising an overnight target. Uncertainty: high, because sampled loop target_bg values span 80 to 116 mg/dL and do not follow the declared schedule, autosens target modulation is disabled, and logged temporary targets explain at most one value, so a declared-target change may not produce the expected effect. Dependencies: the night-stratification check must first establish whether the lows are target-driven or an evening insulin tail. Keep pending that check.

Evidence: the daytime window covered by this target shows 0 to 1.8 percent time below range from 08:00 to 12:00 local and no hypoglycemia pressure, while the afternoon elevation is attributable to unannounced carbohydrate. Uncertainty: the effective loop target in this window was observed as low as 80 mg/dL, which is unexplained and is itself a contributor to correction aggression at high glucose. Dependencies: the target discrepancy is not represented in decision_inventory and cannot be resolved by changing the declared value; keep and observe.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows 10.1 percent time below range and an average of 105.7 mg/dL while descending from the evening rise. Uncertainty: high, for the same reason as the 00:00 target: effective loop targets do not track the declared schedule, so the causal link between this declared value and the observed lows is not established. Dependencies: this segment shares its cause with the 00:00 target and the evening insulin tail, and only one of the three can be changed at a time. Keep pending the night-stratification check.

Evidence: DIA of 10 hours with a free-peak insulin model flattens decay and is mechanistically implicated in carrying afternoon insulin into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster and evening insulin into the overnight cluster, alongside observed insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.935 units. Uncertainty: high, because DIA cannot be validated without a clean fasting decay curve after a single bolus with no subsequent intake, and no such window exists in the supplied response windows, which are all non-monotonic and imply unlogged food. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change insulin-on-board accounting across every other proposed step simultaneously, which is exactly the dependent-change pattern to avoid. Keep, and reconsider only if the max_iob and sensitivity steps fail to reduce the evening lows.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB reported as 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses, UAM is the only mechanism providing meal coverage, and aggregate outcomes remain good at 86.0 percent time in range and 32.6 percent coefficient of variation. Uncertainty: the identified problem is the magnitude and timing of UAM dosing, not its existence. Dependencies: disabling either switch would remove all meal coverage and would very likely worsen the afternoon and evening hyperglycemia; the appropriate levers are the sensitivity factor and the SMB interval. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: smb_always_enabled true makes the COB-related switches functionally inert, and they are doubly inert because no carbohydrates were entered; there is no internal contradiction in the group. The high-temporary-target gate did suppress SMB during 180-minute targets of 135 mg/dL on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, accounting for roughly 435 minutes out of 336 hours. Uncertainty: that exposure explains part of the elevation on those two days but not the 14-day afternoon pattern. Dependencies: enabling SMB under high temporary targets would remove a deliberate brake in a system already showing insulin accumulation to 5.935 units, so change is unsupported. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=5 to 8 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: a 3-minute interval against a 5-minute CGM cadence permits a microbolus on essentially every loop cycle, and observed insulin on board reached 4.73 units on 2026-08-19 and 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 against roughly 16 to 20 units per day, with post-correction drops of minus 168 and minus 178 mg/dL in 120 minutes. Uncertainty: medium. The same overshoots are equally consistent with the 27.8 to 43 mg/dL per unit effective sensitivity at high glucose, so frequency and per-dose strength are not yet separated; in addition the declared minute caps do not appear to bound delivered SMB size in this build, since reason strings record 0.4 unit microboluses and one 1.6 unit boosted SMB against a cap implying roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units, which is why only the interval component is proposed for change and the two minute caps are left as they are. Dependencies: this must be tested strictly after and separately from the dynamic sensitivity change and the max_iob change; changing it in parallel would make the result uninterpretable. All three components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: max_iob of 25 units exceeds the entire estimated daily insulin requirement of roughly 16 to 20 units and is about four times the highest insulin on board observed, 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 at 245.7 mg/dL with an effective target of 80 and sensitivity of 27.8; no sequence of dosing in this dataset could ever have reached the limit, so it provides no practical ceiling in a system that produced 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. The max_basal component is left unchanged because the effective ceiling is the derived maxSafeBasal of 3.0 to 4.2 U/h, confirmed twice in the logs, so 12 U/h is already non-binding and lowering it would not change delivery. Uncertainty: low for the direction, moderate for the exact value, since true total daily dose is unknown because delivered basal is not summed anywhere in the package; the candidate range is therefore deliberately set well above observed peak usage. Dependencies: this is a guard rather than a dose-calculation input, so it is the least entangled change and is sequenced first, before the sensitivity and SMB interval steps. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

suggested_value: autosens_enabled=false; dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true; autosens_raises_target=false; autosens_lowers_target=false; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=55 to 60 %
rationale: Evidence: the four switches are internally consistent, since dynamic sensitivity supersedes autosens and both autosens target switches correctly follow autosens being disabled, so none of them is proposed for change. The adjustment factor of 70 percent, however, produces effective sensitivity from 124.0 mg/dL per unit at 69.8 mg/dL with negative insulin on board down to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL with 5.935 units on board, roughly a two-fold swing in each direction around the flat 56 anchor, which matches the observed pattern of weak correction across the 130 to 160 mg/dL plateau and roughly double-strength dosing above 200 mg/dL followed by 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. Uncertainty: medium. Sampled sensitivity ratios include restraining values of 0.79 to 0.94, showing the layer is not one-directional, and only 24 of 6214 device statuses were supplied so the sensitivity values are a sample rather than a distribution; GLP-1 dosing on 2026-08-14, 08-17, and 08-20 may also have shifted true sensitivity mid-window. Dependencies: must be tested separately from the SMB interval change and after the max_iob guard, because all three act on the same overshoot evidence. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: both parameters govern COB decay and meal absorption modelling, and COB was reported as 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, extended_carb_entries 0, and average_extended_carb_duration_min null, so neither value influenced a single dosing decision in the period. Uncertainty: this is a keep because change is unsupported, not because the values are validated; no evidence exists in either direction, and no absorption duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: if carbohydrate logging begins as proposed, these two values, min_carbs_required_grams, the COB-related activation switches, and the carb ratio segments all become live at once, which is precisely the simultaneous dependent change the workflow forbids; they should therefore be reviewed only after several announced meals exist. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Local hours 00 and 01 show averages of 93.3 and 90.6 mg/dL with 0.0 percent above range but 11.4 and 18.5 percent below range, which does indicate low-glucose exposure. However the evidence does not separate a basal cause from the 10 h DIA tail of evening dosing, from the 90 mg/dL target segment, or from carry-over of the afternoon over-correction chain, and four of five sampled late-evening correction windows undershoot 3 to 4 hours later. Uncertainty is raised further by the absence of any continuous insulin on board series, only 24 of 6214 device statuses being exposed. Dependency: this window is downstream of the same automation chain targeted by the max IOB and dynamic sensitivity steps, so a basal change here would confound both.

Local hour 05 averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range, 0.0 percent above range and 4.8 percent below range, and local hour 06 averages 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 percent in range. This is near-target and stable in a fasting-like window, so there is no evidence supporting a change. Uncertainty is low for this specific window because it is the least confounded part of the day. Dependency: none that would alter this conclusion.

Local hours 07, 08 and 09 average 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL with 98.7, 98.2 and 91.1 percent time in range and 0.0 to 1.3 percent below range. The rise from 99.5 mg/dL at hour 07 to 148.0 mg/dL at hour 10 is real, but with carb entries at 0 it cannot be separated from an unlogged breakfast, and labelling it a basal defect is not supportable. Uncertainty is high on the cause of the rise and low on the safety of the current value. Dependency: resolution requires the carbohydrate logging observation, which is sequenced after the automation steps.

Local hours 10 to 13 average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3 and 135.0 mg/dL with time above range of 20.2, 7.5, 14.0 and 16.6 percent, so this window does contribute to the daytime elevation. However the sampled loop statuses show the elevation is met with temp basal rates up to 3.6 U/h and boosted microboluses rather than with the profile rate, so the profile value is not the acting constraint. Uncertainty is high because unlogged meals remain a plausible full explanation. Dependency: cannot be separated from the automation gain steps, which act on the same hours.

This is the lowest basal segment in the profile and it sits inside the worst hyperglycemia block, with local hours 16 and 17 averaging 162.8 and 148.9 mg/dL at 32.1 and 22.6 percent above range. That co-location is the single most suggestive profile finding. It is nonetheless withheld from change for three reasons: with carb entries at 0 an unlogged afternoon meal explains the same pattern; the reduction may be deliberately protecting the immediately following 18:00 to 19:59 local window where both level 2 hypoglycemia clusters occurred at 42 and 41 mg/dL; and raising it would act on exactly the same window as the two automation steps. Dependency: revisit only after both automation steps have been observed and after the afternoon window has been re-examined on days without a preceding hypoglycemia rebound.

Local hour 18 shows 7.7 percent below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, so this is a genuine risk window. However the two level 2 clusters here on 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14 each followed a documented afternoon high with an aggressive automation response 2 to 5 hours earlier, including a 0.2 U dose at 17:20 local on 2026-08-14 that preceded 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes, so the delivered insulin came predominantly from automation rather than from this basal rate. Uncertainty about attribution is high. Dependency: the max IOB and dynamic sensitivity steps target this exact mechanism and must be evaluated before any basal change here.

Local hour 19 has the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and this segment is a rate increase relative to the preceding hour, which makes it a plausible contributor. It is still withheld because the same window is the terminal point of the chase-then-crash chain identified from the therapy response windows, and because glucose recovers well immediately afterwards, with local hours 20, 21 and 22 at 88.6, 92.3 and 86.2 percent in range. Reducing this rate now would remove the ability to attribute any improvement to the automation steps. Dependency: strictly sequenced after both automation steps.

Carb entries are 0, total carbs are 0.0 g and the carb treatment entries list is empty, so this segment was never invoked during the period and no element of the package can confirm or refute it. The carb ratio values appearing in loop reason strings only confirm which profile segment was loaded. Uncertainty is maximal. No carbohydrate was entered at any time in the 14 day period, so this segment produced no observable effect and cannot be evaluated. Bolus wizard percentage is 100 and minimum required carbs is 20 g, neither of which was ever engaged. Uncertainty is maximal. Dependency: requires carbohydrate logging before any assessment is possible.

This segment covers the 07:00 to 10:00 local rise from 99.5 to 148.0 mg/dL, which is the most likely morning eating window, but with 0 carb entries there is no meal-linked evidence to test the ratio against. All 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses, not meal boluses. Uncertainty is maximal. Dependency: requires the carbohydrate logging observation to become testable.

This is the most aggressive carb ratio in the profile and it covers the worst excursion block from local hours 16 to 19, which makes it a natural suspect, but it was never invoked because carb entries are 0. Attributing the afternoon pattern to it would be inference without any meal-linked evidence. Uncertainty is maximal. Dependency: this is the specific segment the recommended carbohydrate logging observation would unblock first.

No carbohydrate was entered during the period, so this segment had no observable effect. The evening hours it covers, local 20 to 22, are among the better-controlled hours at 88.6, 92.3 and 86.2 percent time in range, giving no independent reason to suspect it. Uncertainty is maximal on the value itself. Dependency: requires carbohydrate logging before assessment.

Dynamic sensitivity is enabled and Autosens is disabled, so the operative sensitivity is the variable value, which ranged from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U across the sampled statuses. The static 56 mg/dL/U therefore acts as a scaling anchor rather than the acting parameter, and changing it would shift the entire dynamic curve in a way that cannot be predicted from this package. No clean ISF test exists because every one of the 24 correction windows overlaps concurrent temp basal and microbolus activity, for example a 0.2 U dose associated with a 178 mg/dL fall on 2026-08-14, which no ISF value could produce. Dependency: the dynamic ISF adjustment factor is the correct lever for this behaviour and must be tried first and alone.

Local hours 00 to 03 show time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent with essentially no time above range, so a higher overnight target is a plausible future option. It is withheld because the sampled loop statuses show the loop does not consistently use the declared segments, reporting targets of 80 to 116 mg/dL, so raising the declared value may not produce the expected effect until the dynamic target mechanism is understood. Uncertainty about the acting target is high. Dependency: the target question should be resolved after the dynamic sensitivity step, and the overnight window is also downstream of the DIA tail.

This segment covers the entire afternoon elevation and early evening low window, but the sampled loop statuses repeatedly show an acting target of 80 mg/dL during exactly the high or rising states within this segment, on 2026-08-10, 2026-08-18, 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-21, while both Autosens target flags are false and the recorded temporary targets are 135 and 108 mg/dL. Raising the declared value is therefore of uncertain effect while an un-inventoried dynamic target mechanism is overriding it. Dependency: clarify the dynamic target behaviour in the running build before considering any declared target change.

Local hour 23 shows 10.1 percent below range and 1.2 percent above range, and four of five sampled late-evening correction windows undershoot, including 125 to 68 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 2026-08-17. This is consistent with a slightly low evening target but is equally consistent with the 10 h DIA tail and with small manual corrections given at near-normal glucose. Uncertainty about separation is high. Dependency: should be considered only after the max IOB and dynamic sensitivity steps, and never together with the 00:00 target segment.

A 10 h DIA is long and is consistent with the observed 6 hour changes of minus 176 and minus 173 mg/dL and with insulin on board reaching 5.935 U with zero carbs on board. However those windows started at 234 and 264 mg/dL, so regression to the mean plus boost magnitude produces the same shape, and the free peak insulin model peak time is not exposed in the package, so the decay curve cannot be reconstructed. Uncertainty is therefore high. Dependency: DIA also inflates reported insulin on board and so interacts directly with the recommended max IOB change; changing both in one cycle would make the max IOB observation uninterpretable.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is not available. With carb entries at 0 and carbs on board at 0 in every sampled status, UAM is the sole meal detection mechanism and SMB is the sole meal coverage mechanism, so disabling either would remove all meal coverage from a system that currently achieves 86.0 percent time in range. UAM is not treated here as duplicate carbohydrate counting, since no carbohydrate is ever entered. Uncertainty is low for this decision. Dependency: the problematic magnitude comes from boost logic and dynamic sensitivity, not from these two switches, so the correct levers are elsewhere.

All five components have non-null values, so verify is not available. The group is internally coherent: smb_always_enabled true makes the two carbohydrate-conditional flags functionally moot, which is doubly true with 0 carb entries. Crucially, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false converts the user temporary targets of 135 mg/dL recorded on 2026-08-09, 17, 18, 19 and 20 into a working manual microbolus brake over the highest-risk afternoon and evening window, including a 180 minute target from 15:24 local on 2026-08-18. Removing that brake would increase risk in exactly the window containing the two level 2 hypoglycemia clusters. Dependency: none that supports a change; this group should stay fixed while the max IOB and dynamic sensitivity steps are evaluated.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: All three components have non-null values, so verify is not available. These values are already more conservative than AAPS defaults of 30 and 30 minutes, with a standard 3 minute interval, and no SMB interval was inferred from any remaining-time text in the loop reasons. The decisive evidence against tightening them is that they are not the binding constraint: on 2026-08-07 the loop recorded a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U and microbolused 0.4 U, and on 2026-08-19 at 15:54 UTC a UAM High Boost delivered an SMB of 1.6 U. Reducing these caps would therefore penalise normal small microboluses without limiting the peaks that matter. Uncertainty is medium because the boost logic is not in the inventory. Dependency: the max IOB backstop and the dynamic sensitivity factor are the reviewable levers that do act on peak delivery.

Both components have non-null values. Evidence: total insulin is 275.95 U over 14 days, approximately 19.7 U per day, so a max IOB of 25 U exceeds a full day of insulin and cannot function as a limit; the largest observed insulin on board was 5.935 U at 2026-08-21 21:09 UTC and 4.73 U at 2026-08-19 15:54 UTC, both with zero carbs on board and both within or immediately preceding the high-glucose states that lead into the documented early evening lows. A candidate of 10 U sits above roughly 1.7 times the worst observed stacking event, so it is expected to be inert in normal operation while restoring a genuine ceiling. Max basal of 12 U/h is deliberately left unchanged in the same cycle: it is already non-binding because the real ceiling comes from the safety multipliers, evidenced on 2026-08-14 where an adjusted requested rate of 5.9 U/h was clamped to a maximum safe basal of 4 U/h with 3.6 U/h enacted, and changing two components of one group together would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule. Uncertainty: total daily dose composition is unresolved between roughly 20 and 36 U per day, and DIA 10 h inflates reported insulin on board, so the exact value must be confirmed with the care team. Dependency: must be applied before and separately from the dynamic ISF adjustment factor change.

All five components have non-null values, so verify is not available. The four boolean components are kept: Autosens disabled with dynamic sensitivity enabled under the oref1 algorithm is a coherent pairing, and the observed sensitivity ratios of 0.79 to 0.98 come from the dynamic path while a ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment rather than a disabled feature. Only the adjustment factor is proposed for change. Evidence: variable sensitivity ranged from 124.0 mg/dL/U at 69.8 mg/dL to 27.8 mg/dL/U at 245.7 mg/dL, and at 2026-08-21 21:09 UTC the loop combined a target of 80 mg/dL with a sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL/U to request 2.12 U at a 4 U/h rate with 5.935 U already on board and zero carbs on board, roughly 1.45 times what target 100 and ISF 56 would imply; the downstream cost is visible as 4 of 9 corrections started at or above 165 mg/dL falling below 70 mg/dL within 6 hours. Uncertainty is significant: this build shows several non-inventoried features and the direction convention of the adjustment factor is not stated in the package, so the convention must be confirmed in the running build before applying, and 60 percent is a single conservative step rather than a target value. Dependency: apply only after the max IOB observation period, alone, and never together with any basal, target or DIA change because all act on the same afternoon-to-evening window.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is not available and a missing-data status is not applicable. These settings govern carbs-on-board decomposition and Autosens meal exclusion, and both are functionally inert in this period because carbs on board is 0 in every sampled status and Autosens is disabled. No evidence in the package can support or refute either value; 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes is the standard default and 7 h is modestly above a typical 6 h. This is a keep on absence of applicable evidence rather than on demonstrated correctness. Dependency: these values acquire real meaning only if carbohydrate entry begins, at which point a 7 h absorption ceiling combined with DIA 10 h would extend carbohydrate-driven dosing into the 18:00 to 19:59 local low window and should be re-evaluated at that time.

Evidence is mixed rather than absent. Local hour 00:00 shows 11.4 percent and 01:00 shows 18.5 percent time below range, which superficially suggests excess. Against this, mean glucose rises from 90.6 at 01:00 to 106.0 at 04:00 while time below range falls to 3.0 percent, a pattern that fits decaying evening insulin on board under a 10-hour DIA rather than an excessive overnight rate. Uncertainty: evening corrections at 21:51 to 22:30 local were still suppressing glucose at 360 minutes, so carry-over cannot be separated from the basal rate. Dependencies: the maximum insulin on board guardrail and the Dynamic ISF curve both act on this window and are sequenced ahead of any basal change.

Evidence supports no change: local hour 05:00 shows a mean of 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range, 0.0 percent above and 4.8 percent below. Uncertainty: this hour is also the tail of the overnight insulin on board carry-over, so its apparent adequacy is partly a product of upstream events rather than proof that the rate is correct. Dependencies: none that would justify acting here before the guardrail and the meal announcement steps.

Evidence: local hours 06:00 and 07:00 show means of 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 and 98.7 percent time in range and near-zero time above range, so the early part of the highest basal segment performs well. The rise to 132.9 at 09:00 and 148.0 at 10:00 begins inside this segment, but with zero carbohydrate entries a morning meal is at least as plausible as a basal deficit. Uncertainty: the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 08-21 preceded a sensor change by two hours, so an artifact cannot be excluded. Dependencies: this segment sets the most permissive SMB caps of the day, about 0.20 and 0.267 U, so raising it would also increase automation aggressiveness.

Evidence: this segment spans hourly means of 132.3 to 162.8 mg/dL with 7.5 to 32.1 percent time above range, which would superficially argue for an increase. The change is withheld because meals are entirely unannounced and carbohydrates on board are 0 throughout, so the elevation cannot be separated from post-meal excursions handled late by UAM. Uncertainty: the afternoons of 08-17 and 08-18 inside this segment contained 180-minute SMB blackouts from 135 mg/dL temporary targets and are excluded from inference. Dependencies: any increase would also raise the SMB caps and the current-basal safety ceiling feeding into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia window.

Evidence: this is the strongest apparent mismatch, since the lowest basal of the day sits under 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and 148.9 mg/dL at 17:00 with 22.6 percent above range. The change is withheld for a mechanical reason: SMB caps are expressed in minutes of profile basal, so raising this segment to 0.7 U per hour would lift the UAM SMB ceiling from about 0.167 to 0.233 U and raise the current-basal safety ceiling, increasing aggressiveness immediately before the 18:00 and 19:00 hours that already carry 7.7 and 15.3 percent time below range. Uncertainty: unannounced afternoon meals remain a fully plausible alternative explanation. Dependencies: this row cannot be isolated from aaps.core.smb_delivery or from the Dynamic ISF curve.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL on the steep descent from the afternoon peak, and the lows follow boosted corrections rather than a steady basal excess, for example the 08-14 window falling from 234 to 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes after 1.3 U was delivered within 10 minutes. Uncertainty: a basal contribution cannot be excluded, only deprioritized. Dependencies: the Dynamic ISF curve and the maximum insulin on board ceiling both act on this descent and are sequenced first.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 carries the second highest time below range of the period at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the highest evening basal begins exactly here, so this is a genuine candidate. The change is withheld because the same hour follows the afternoon peak and its boosted corrections, and because four of four evening correction windows drifted low with no preceding rise, implicating insulin on board carry-over under a 10-hour DIA alongside the basal rate. Uncertainty: basal and carry-over cannot be separated with the current data. Dependencies: this is the highest-priority basal row to revisit once the maximum insulin on board ceiling has been observed for 14 days, and it should be examined before any other basal segment.

Evidence: unfalsifiable in this period, because carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board are 0 in all 24 sampled statuses, so no bolus-to-carbohydrate outcome exists for this segment. Uncertainty: loop reason strings repeatedly report 13.3 g per unit in this window against the profile value of 13.0, about 2 percent, which suggests the running configuration may differ from the reviewed profile and is worth confirming, though it is not itself a reason to change the value. Dependencies: becomes assessable only after carbohydrate announcement begins.

Evidence: unfalsifiable, because zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrates on board 0 mean no meal response can be attributed to this segment. The value is confirmed consistent between profile and loop output, which reports 11.1 in this window. Uncertainty: no outcome data at all exists for this ratio. Dependencies: requires the meal announcement step before any assessment is possible.

Evidence: unfalsifiable, despite this segment covering the most reproducible excursion in the dataset, the rise from 99.5 mg/dL at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 local. With no carbohydrate entered there is no calculated bolus and no measurable ratio, and the value matches loop output of 13.2. Uncertainty: nothing resolvable from this package. Dependencies: this is the segment that the proposed morning meal announcement would make measurable first, and it should be the first carb ratio examined once 7 to 10 days of paired data exist.

Evidence: unfalsifiable. This is the strongest carb ratio of the day and covers the highest-glucose hours, but with zero carbohydrate entries there is no way to test it. The value matches loop output of 10.5. Uncertainty: the elevation in this window is confounded by unannounced meals, by the 180-minute SMB blackouts on 08-17 and 08-18, and by the Dynamic ISF curve being weakest in exactly this glucose band. Dependencies: assessment requires both meal announcement and resolution of the sensitivity question.

Evidence: unfalsifiable, because zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrates on board 0 mean no evening meal response can be attributed here. The value matches loop output of 12.6. Uncertainty: the evening window shows a distinct downward drift, with four of four correction windows falling and no preceding rise, but that is a basal, DIA and insulin on board pattern and must not be attributed to a carb ratio. Dependencies: requires meal announcement before assessment.

Evidence: the static value is never used directly for dosing. With Dynamic ISF enabled at a 70 percent factor and Autosens disabled, observed effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit, crossing 56 only near 170 to 190 mg/dL, with 124 at 70 mg/dL, 108 at 84, 71 to 87 at 120 to 140 and 27.8 to 37.9 at 245 to 262. Changing the base would shift the whole curve, including the protective high sensitivity at low glucose, which would work against the primary problem of 5.1 percent time below range. Uncertainty: whether the curve shape or the base is at fault cannot be separated without knowing this build sign convention. Dependencies: inseparable from aaps.core.sensitivity, and only one of the two may be touched, with the automation group being the correct target.

Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 carry 10.1 to 18.5 percent time below range, which would ordinarily argue for raising the overnight target. The change is blocked because the effective target used by the loop is not derivable from this row: observed values include 80, 84, 86, 87, 96.4 and 97 mg/dL, and 80 appears on the most aggressive high-glucose loops, below the profile floor, while Autosens target adjustment is disabled in both directions. Uncertainty: raising a row that is being overridden by an unidentified mechanism could produce no effect or an unpredictable one. Dependencies: blocked until the source of the sub-profile target is identified.

Evidence: this daytime target covers the safest window in the dataset, with 0.0 percent time below range at 08:00 and 09:00 local, so there is no hypoglycemia argument for raising it, and the afternoon time above range is better explained by the sensitivity curve and unannounced meals than by the target. Uncertainty: the same override problem applies, with effective targets of 80 mg/dL observed on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21 within this segment. Dependencies: blocked until the source of the sub-profile target is identified.

Evidence: local hour 23:00 shows 10.1 percent time below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL, so a higher late-evening target is a plausible future direction. The change is withheld for the same override reason as the other target rows, and because the evening lows are better attributed to insulin on board carry-over from corrections at 21:51 to 22:30 local that were still suppressing glucose at 360 minutes. Uncertainty: target, basal and carry-over all act on the same hours and are not separated. Dependencies: blocked until the sub-profile target source is identified and until the maximum insulin on board guardrail has been observed.

Evidence: DIA of 10 hours with free_peak_oref produces a long tail, and the largest observed falls occur at 240 to 360 minutes rather than 120 minutes, which initially suggested DIA as a candidate. That reasoning is corrected here, because a longer DIA is conservative by design, counting more insulin on board at dosing time, so shortening it would make the algorithm dose more, which is the wrong direction against 5.1 percent time below range. The magnitude of the falls is explained by dose size at the peak under an effective sensitivity of 27.8 to 37.9 mg/dL per unit above 200 mg/dL. Uncertainty: the insulin peak time is not exposed, so the modeled tail shape cannot be verified. Dependencies: DIA amplifies the evening carry-over in the 19:00 to 03:00 window and should be revisited only after the sensitivity and basal questions are settled.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable and the decision is keep. Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days, UAM is the only mechanism responding to meals, and disabling it would remove the sole meal response and would predictably worsen the 14.0 to 32.1 percent time above range in the 12:00 to 17:00 local band; 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U were delivered with carbohydrates on board 0 throughout. The two components are mutually consistent and consistent with smb_always_enabled true. Uncertainty: none material for this group. Dependencies: the problem lies in dose size, governed by aaps.core.sensitivity and the custom boost logic, not in enablement.

All five components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable. Evidence: the set is internally consistent, since smb_always_enabled true makes the carbohydrates on board and after-carbs conditions dormant, and they are doubly dormant with zero carbohydrate entries. One material behavior is documented rather than changed: with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, the 135 mg/dL temporary targets of 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18 suppressed SMB entirely, and on 08-17 glucose rose from 126 to 190 mg/dL across that interval before falling to 111 and 95 mg/dL when SMB resumed. Uncertainty: the intent behind each temporary target is unknown, and the user appears to be using high targets deliberately as a manual brake. suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: All three components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable. Evidence: the two basal-minute caps are already below the common 30-minute defaults and are demonstrably not binding, since the 20-minute UAM allowance corresponds to about 0.167 U at the 16:00 basal of 0.5 U per hour yet a UAM High Boost delivered 1.6 U on 08-19 at 264 mg/dL, and on 08-07 the reason string states standardMaxBolus 0.2 while microbolusing 0.4 U. Lowering caps that are already overridden would create the appearance of restraint without the substance. Uncertainty: the magnitude of the custom boost multipliers is unquantified and outside decision_inventory, so the true ceiling on a single SMB cannot be derived. Dependencies: these caps scale with profile basal, so they are coupled to every basal row, and the 3-minute interval is retained as a secondary candidate only if the sensitivity lever is declined, never changed alongside the maximum insulin on board ceiling.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable, and change applies to the max_iob_units component only while max_basal_u_per_hour is kept. Evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is 15 times the largest profile basal of 0.8 and never binds, because the real ceiling in the logs is a maximum safe basal of 4 U per hour produced by the safety multipliers, so lowering 12 would be inert until it fell below 4, at which point it would become a dependent change. max_iob_units of 25 is roughly 1.5 times the entire daily profile basal of 16.2 U and never engaged, while observed insulin on board reached 4.73 U on 08-19 and 5.935 U on 08-21, both with carbohydrates on board 0, the latter at an effective sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit with a further 2.12 U requested, and four of nine correction windows starting above 160 mg/dL fell below 60 mg/dL within six hours. A ceiling of 8 U sits above all routine operation while capping the two extreme accumulation episodes. Uncertainty: the exact value depends on the basal versus bolus split of total daily dose, which cannot be computed from the 40 sampled treatments, so 8 U is a supported starting point for discussion rather than a derived optimum. Dependencies: this is the only lever independent of all profile rows and of the Dynamic ISF curve, which is why it is sequenced first and alone.

All five components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable and the decision must be change or keep. Evidence: this group contains the best-supported mechanism in the analysis, since the effective sensitivity curve is weak through the sustained 130 to 163 mg/dL afternoon band and strong above 200 mg/dL, crossing the static profile ISF near 170 to 190 mg/dL, matching 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 followed by 15.3 percent below range at 19:00. Keep is nonetheless correct now for two reasons: the sign convention of dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent differs between builds and this branch contains undocumented boost logic, so change may not be used without a supported value, and this group is dependent on the profile ISF row and on profile basal so it cannot be changed in the same step as the maximum insulin on board ceiling. Interpretation note: sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.00 are read as neutral or mildly reduced current adjustments from the dynamic path, not as a disabled Autosens and not as duplicate counting. Uncertainty: three GLP-1 doses within seven days make the period non-stationary. Dependencies: sequenced third, after the guardrail and the meal announcement have each been observed separately.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable. Evidence: both settings act on carbohydrates on board, which is 0 in every sampled loop status, with zero carbohydrate entries and zero extended carbohydrate entries in 14 days, so they are entirely dormant and nothing in this package can support a change in either direction; min_5m_carbimpact of 8 is also the common default. Uncertainty: none resolvable while the settings are dormant, and no duration is inferred from average_extended_carb_duration_min because it is null. Dependencies: a forward-looking caveat is recorded that a 7-hour maximum absorption combined with a 10-hour DIA would create long overlapping carbohydrate and insulin tails once announcement begins, which becomes assessable only after 7 to 10 days of announced meals produce a real absorption curve.

Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 show 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent below range, which looks like basal excess, but lows recur despite frequent zero-rate temporary basals of 10 to 55 minutes, meaning delivery was already suspended when the lows occurred. Uncertainty: the preceding evening carries a 10-hour DIA tail plus boosted UAM dosing, so the responsible insulin was delivered hours earlier. Dependencies: this row cannot be separated from dynamic ISF, max IOB and the absence of carbohydrate announcement, all of which are addressed earlier in the sequence; lowering it now would add a second simultaneous change and would probably not remove the cause.

Evidence: local hour 05:00 averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range and 4.8 percent below range, and hour 06:00 averages 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 percent in range, which is the best-performing window of the day. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment, since it sits in the only genuinely fasting-like period. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; altering a well-behaved segment would add noise to the verification of the earlier steps.

Evidence: local hours 06:00 and 07:00 average 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 and 98.7 percent in range and only 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range. Uncertainty: an isolated 42 mg/dL at 08-21 07:19 local sits in an otherwise low-risk hour and may be a sensor artefact, so it does not support a reduction. Dependencies: this is the largest basal segment and therefore sets the observed automation clamp of 4 U/h through the daily safety multiplier of 5.0, so any change here would silently move an automation limit as well and must not be combined with automation changes.

Evidence: local hours 10:00 to 13:00 average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3 and 135.0 mg/dL with time above range from 7.5 to 20.2 percent, which could suggest under-basalisation. Uncertainty: no carbohydrate was entered in the period, so unannounced breakfast and midday eating is at least as plausible an explanation as the basal rate, and the loop already responds with temporary basals up to 2.7 U/h in this window. Dependencies: separating these two explanations requires the carbohydrate logging step first; a basal increase now would also raise insulin exposure ahead of the 18:00 to 19:00 low window.

Evidence: local hour 16:00 is the highest of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and zero percent below range, and it coincides exactly with the lowest scheduled basal segment. Uncertainty: this coincidence is not attributable to the basal rate, because automation already reaches its maxSafeBasal clamp of 4 U/h in this window, so additional scheduled basal would be partly redundant, and unannounced afternoon eating remains an equally plausible driver. Dependencies: the constraint that no change may increase insulin exposure between 14:00 and 03:00 local applies directly here, since this window feeds the 18:00 to 19:00 low period with 15.3 percent below range; the fasting observation named in profile_recommendation must resolve this first.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 shows 7.7 percent below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the step up from 0.5 to 0.6 U/h occurs at this boundary. Uncertainty: the level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 both began in this hour but followed high-glucose afternoons with boosted SMB and temporary basal, so the causal insulin was delivered earlier and is carried by the 10-hour DIA tail rather than by this segment. Dependencies: reducing this row would treat a symptom of the upstream accumulation identified in the automation stages and would confound the verification of the max IOB step.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 has the highest low-glucose exposure of the day at 15.3 percent below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, while averaging 105.4 mg/dL. Uncertainty: as in the 18:00 segment, zero-rate temporary basals were frequently already active when these lows occurred, which points to insulin-on-board of 4.7 to 5.9 U rather than to the scheduled rate. Dependencies: this is the strongest single candidate for a later basal reduction, but only if low glucose in this hour persists after carbohydrate logging and the max IOB review; changing it now would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule and mask which step produced any improvement.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so this ratio was never applied to any dose during the period. Uncertainty: complete, since no observation exists that could support or refute the value. Dependencies: blocked by the meal_ecarbs_absorption stage; it becomes assessable only after the carbohydrate logging step produces paired carbohydrate and glucose data.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists in the period and COB is zero throughout, so this segment was never exercised. Uncertainty: complete; the 04:00 to 08:00 window is also the quietest eating period, so it will be the last segment to gain evidence. Dependencies: requires carbohydrate logging before any assessment is possible.

Evidence: the morning rise from 99.5 mg/dL at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 local is consistent with unannounced breakfast, but with zero carbohydrate entries this ratio never acted on it. Uncertainty: dawn physiology and unannounced eating cannot be separated, and there is zero percent below range in these hours, so no safety pressure exists. Dependencies: assessment requires the carbohydrate logging step and, if breakfast is the recurring occasion chosen, this is the segment most likely to gain evidence first.

Evidence: this is the strongest ratio in the schedule and it aligns with the highest-glucose window at 16:00 local (162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range), yet it was never applied because no carbohydrate was announced. Uncertainty: complete regarding the ratio itself; the window's behaviour is currently explained by reactive UAM dosing rather than by any carbohydrate calculation. Dependencies: blocked by the absence of carbohydrate entries, and any future evaluation must also account for the low-glucose constraint in the following hours.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists, so this segment never contributed to a dose; the evening pattern is dominated instead by carried insulin-on-board and small manual corrections such as 0.05 U at BG 245 with 5.94 U already on board on 08-21. Uncertainty: complete for the ratio. Dependencies: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists, and any evening change would additionally interact with the 22:00 to 03:00 low window.

Evidence: dynamic sensitivity is enabled with autosens disabled, and observed variable_sens ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, so the flat profile value is only one input to a glucose and insulin-on-board scaled calculation rather than the operative sensitivity. Uncertainty: the build formula and its neutral point are not supplied, so the effect of moving 56 in either direction cannot be predicted from the package. Dependencies: strictly coupled to the dynamic ISF adjustment factor; changing both would be a simultaneous change of dependent parameters, and the automation-side factor is the more direct lever, so the profile value is held.
