Evidence: logged effective target_bg ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL across sampled statuses while this segment declares 90, and both autosens target flags are false, so the running build is generating the effective target rather than this row. Uncertainty: high, because the mechanism is undocumented and only 24 of 6214 statuses are visible; a change to this row may not propagate as expected. Dependencies: target evidence remains weak until the effective-target mechanism is understood, so no target row may be moved on this data.

Evidence: this daytime target of 100 covers the plateau hours, yet sampled statuses in that window logged effective targets as low as 80 to 82 mg/dL at elevated glucose, which is not explained by this row or by the six temporary targets. Uncertainty: high for the same undocumented mechanism. Dependencies: raising this target could reduce afternoon dosing pressure, but that overlaps directly with the dynamic ISF and max IOB steps and would confound their verification, so it is withheld.

Evidence: this segment covers the 23:00 to 03:00 local window that carries 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, which superficially argues for a higher overnight target. Uncertainty: the sampled statuses show the build already raising the effective target to 105 to 116 mg/dL when low-glucose risk is predicted, so the declared value is not what the loop uses, and the lows persisted despite that. Dependencies: the overnight lows are attributed primarily to insulin carried from the afternoon and evening, so this row is held until the upstream steps are verified.

Evidence: 11 of 23 sampled therapy response windows remain net negative at 360 minutes, for example minus 50, minus 51, minus 66 and minus 176 mg/dL, which is compatible with a long action tail. Uncertainty: those windows always contain concurrent basal, temporary basal and UAM SMB activity, so they cannot isolate insulin decay, and no insulin-free window exists in the period. Dependencies: DIA interacts with the insulin-on-board model that the max IOB step is intended to constrain; shortening DIA would reduce calculated insulin-on-board and could paradoxically increase dosing, so it must not be changed alongside the max IOB review.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB zero in every sampled status, SMB and UAM constitute the entire meal-coverage mechanism, and every sampled dosing decision is UAM-driven. There is no duplicate COB counting because COB is always zero. Uncertainty: whether UAM is over-reacting cannot be separated from the dynamic sensitivity gradient that sizes its requests. Dependencies: disabling either switch would remove all responsiveness to unannounced eating and would predictably worsen the 10:00 to 17:00 local plateau, where time above range reaches 32.1 percent, so both remain enabled while the upstream carbohydrate and ceiling steps are tested. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: smb_always_enabled true makes the two carbohydrate-conditioned flags inert while COB is zero, which is redundancy rather than a defect, and the pairing of smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false is the protective configuration, permitting SMB under ordinary temporary targets while suppressing it under high temporary targets. The user set six temporary targets in the period, and the largest sampled SMB of 1.6 U on 08-19 occurred after the relevant temporary target had expired, so no target was overridden. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 statuses are visible, so the frequency with which the high-target suppression engaged is unknown. Dependencies: the two carbohydrate-conditioned flags become observable only after carbohydrate logging begins, so they must be re-examined after that step rather than changed now. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: with basal of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h the 20-minute UAM allowance implies a base cap near 0.17 to 0.27 U, consistent with the logged standardMaxBolus of 0.2, yet delivered SMB reached 0.4 U under a boost of 1.57 and 1.6 U under UAM High Boost, so boost multipliers that are absent from the settings inventory dominate the delivered size. The 3-minute interval is read directly from raw_settings and not inferred from any waiting message. Uncertainty: because the boost logic and its own caps are undocumented, the effect of reducing the base minutes cannot be predicted precisely. Dependencies: this parameter is downstream of dynamic sensitivity, which determines the insulin requirement that the cap truncates, and it is the only mechanism currently covering the daytime plateau; reducing it before the carbohydrate and max IOB steps would risk trading low glucose for high glucose and would confound attribution. It is therefore held as the last item in the sequence. All components have values, so verify does not apply.

suggested_value: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h; max_iob_units=6 to 8 U for review with the care team
rationale: Evidence: observed peak insulin-on-board was 5.94 U at BG 245.7 on 08-21 and 4.73 U at BG 262 on 08-19, while max IOB is 25 U, roughly 125 percent of an estimated 20 U per day insulin picture and about 1.5 times the 16.2 U per day scheduled basal, so the ceiling was never approached and applied no restraint before the level-2 low clusters of 08-13 and 08-14. Max basal of 12 U/h is left unchanged because it is not the binding limit; the observed clamp is maxSafeBasal 4 U/h derived from the internal daily safety multiplier of 5.0 applied to the largest basal segment of 0.8 U/h. Uncertainty: total daily dose is bounded only between roughly 20 and 36 U per day because it is unclear whether total_insulin_u includes basal, so the suggested range is a discussion range and not a derived value, and a ceiling set too low could blunt legitimate coverage of the daytime plateau. Dependencies: chosen as the first insulin-related step because a ceiling truncates only extreme accumulation without altering routine dosing, and it must be changed alone, before any dynamic ISF or SMB strength change, so its effect on the 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 local windows can be attributed.

Evidence: autosens state is taken from configuration, not inferred from sensitivity_ratio, which is a neutral 1 in 18 of 24 sampled statuses and below 1 in six, values that must arise from the dynamic path since autosens is off. Observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U against a flat profile ISF of 56, and at 27.8 the loop requested 2.12 U where the profile ISF implies roughly half, an excess of about 110 mg/dL of expected fall that matches observed overshoots of minus 178, minus 168 and minus 153 mg/dL beginning in the 14:00 to 17:00 local high window and ending in the 18:00 to 19:00 low window. Uncertainty: this is the leading but not the proven explanation, because unlogged carbohydrate still absorbing at dosing time would justify the same doses with overshoot appearing only when absorption ended, and the build formula and neutral point are not supplied, so the correct direction of a factor change cannot be derived from 70 percent itself. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is designed to separate exactly these two explanations, and the max IOB ceiling is the safer first intervention, so this group is held and reassessed as the second insulin-related step, changed alone if at all. All components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: both parameters act only when COB exceeds zero, and COB is zero in every sampled status with carb_entries 0 and extended_carb_entries 0, so neither parameter influenced any observed outcome in the period. Uncertainty: the observed six to nine hour daytime excursion span is directionally compatible with the 7-hour maximum absorption setting, but it is confounded by overlapping eating occasions, corrections, temporary basals, three GLP-1 doses and the 10-hour DIA tail, and no meal-linked evidence exists, so no duration may be inferred from it. Dependencies: these settings become live the moment carbohydrate is entered, so they must be re-examined after the carbohydrate logging step and never before it. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: the fasting window that this segment covers is stable, with local hours 02:00 to 04:00 averaging 101.9, 104.7 and 106.0 mg/dL and time below range falling from 10.1 to 3.0 percent, and the 23:00-01:00 dip recovers spontaneously to 106.0 mg/dL by 04:00 without any recorded carbohydrate, which fits a decaying insulin tail rather than excess basal. Uncertainty: the early-night dip at 01:00 local carries 18.5 percent below range, so a basal contribution cannot be fully excluded from aggregate data alone. Dependencies: the dip is attributed to evening insulin-on-board of 2.802 U at 22:04 local and 5.935 U at 22:09 local acting across the 10-hour DIA, so this segment must not be changed before the dynamic ISF change is evaluated.

Evidence: local hours 05:00 and 06:00 average 104.2 and 99.5 mg/dL with 95.2 and 97.5 percent in range and only 4.8 and 2.5 percent below range, which is close to ideal for a fasting window. Uncertainty: no fasting or no-bolus day can be isolated because SMB runs continuously, so residual insulin effects cannot be fully separated. Dependencies: none that would justify a change, since this segment is not implicated in either hypoglycemia cluster.

Evidence: this is the highest scheduled segment and the hours it covers are the safest in the day, with 07:00, 08:00 and 09:00 local showing 98.7, 98.2 and 91.1 percent in range and 1.3, 0.0 and 0.0 percent below range. Uncertainty: the 07:00 to 10:00 local rise from 99.5 to 148.0 mg/dL cannot be separated into dawn phenomenon versus an unannounced breakfast because no carbohydrate was logged, so it does not by itself justify more basal here. Dependencies: separating those two explanations requires the carbohydrate-logging observation, so any change is deferred until that data exists.

Evidence: local hours 10:00 to 12:00 average 148.0, 132.3 and 141.3 mg/dL with time below range of only 1.2, 0.6 and 2.8 percent, and the loop already responds to these rises with temporary basal rates of 2.376 to 4.0 U/h, so the scheduled rate is not the operative driver. Uncertainty: the elevated averages could reflect unannounced meals, dawn effects or GLP-1 delayed emptying, and these cannot be separated without carbohydrate data. Dependencies: raising this segment would add to the insulin tail that reaches the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia window through the 10-hour DIA, so it is withheld pending the automation change.

Evidence: this lowest scheduled segment sits over the worst hyperglycemia hours, with 16:00 local at 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, and 17:00 local at 148.9 mg/dL with 22.6 percent above range, which superficially suggests an increase. That inference is rejected because the loop already delivers 2.7 to 4.0 U/h temporary basal in this window, four to eight times the scheduled rate, so the schedule is not limiting delivery. Uncertainty: whether the afternoon rise is a recurring unannounced meal or a basal shortfall remains unresolved. Dependencies: the immediately following hours carry the most severe hypoglycemia in the dataset, with 41, 42, 45 and 47 mg/dL recorded and 15.3 percent below range at 19:00 local, and both hypoglycemia clusters are traced to afternoon dosing, so adding basal here would very likely deepen those lows and a change must wait for carbohydrate logging and for the dynamic ISF result.

Evidence: this hour carries 7.7 percent below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, which initially suggested reducing basal, but the lows are traceable to earlier doses rather than to this segment, since 0.2 U at 14:05 local on 08-13 produced 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes, which is the 18:05 local extreme. The scheduled rate of 0.6 U/h contributes only 0.05 U per 5 minutes and cannot account for falls of 125 to 178 mg/dL. Uncertainty: unlogged activity is plausible, since 180-minute temporary targets of 135 mg/dL were set on 08-17 and 08-18. Dependencies: this segment is exonerated in favour of the dynamic ISF and DIA mechanism, so it stays unchanged while that mechanism is addressed first.

Evidence: 19:00 local is the worst hypoglycemia hour at 15.3 percent below range with minima of 41 mg/dL, and basal rises into it, which is directionally unhelpful. However the specific episodes are attributable to prior dosing, since 0.2 U at 17:20 local on 08-14 gave a 120-minute change of -178 mg/dL reaching 56 mg/dL, directly preceding the 19:04-19:14 local 41 mg/dL readings. Uncertainty: a small basal contribution cannot be excluded, and unlogged rescue carbohydrate makes the true depth of these episodes unknown. Dependencies: because the causal insulin arrives from the afternoon through a 10-hour DIA amplified by dynamic ISF, changing this segment now would confound the evaluation of the primary automation change, and it is the first profile candidate to revisit if evening lows persist afterwards.

Evidence: this segment is confirmed active because CR 13.0 and neighbouring values appear in loop reasons at the correct local times, but it was never used for dosing, since carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is 0 in every sampled cycle. Uncertainty: correctness is entirely unknown, so this is a keep on untestability rather than on demonstrated accuracy. Dependencies: it becomes testable only after carbohydrate logging begins, as proposed in the observation-only recommendation.

Evidence: confirmed active, since CR 11.1 appears in the loop reason at 04:01 local on 08-09, but no carbohydrate was ever entered in the period so it never influenced a dose. Uncertainty: correctness unknown and untestable from this dataset. Dependencies: requires carbohydrate logging plus a meal actually occurring in the 04:00-08:00 local window, which the glucose pattern does not suggest is common.

Evidence: confirmed active in loop reasons at 09:11 and 15:00 local, yet unused because no carbohydrate was logged. The 07:00 to 10:00 local rise to 148.0 mg/dL would be the natural test case but is currently indistinguishable from dawn phenomenon. Uncertainty: correctness unknown. Dependencies: the morning window is the lowest-hypoglycemia-risk window in the day at 0.0 percent below range at 08:00 and 09:00 local, so it is the safest place to test this ratio once meals are logged.

Evidence: confirmed active in the loop reason at 16:54 local on 08-19, and unused because no carbohydrate was logged. Uncertainty: this is the tightest ratio in the profile and it sits over the hour with the highest time above range at 16:00 local with 32.1 percent, but immediately before the most severe hypoglycemia window at 19:00 local with 15.3 percent below range, so if announcement began it would dose hardest into the riskiest tail, which is a caution about future testing rather than a present finding. Dependencies: must not be adjusted before carbohydrate logging provides real absorption and response data.

Evidence: confirmed active in loop reasons at 22:16 local on 08-07 and 22:09 local on 08-21, and unused because no carbohydrate was logged. Uncertainty: correctness unknown. Dependencies: the evening window already shows an insulin tail into 23:00-03:00 local at 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, so any future evening carbohydrate dosing test should follow the automation change rather than precede it.

Evidence: with dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true at a 70 percent adjustment factor and Autosens disabled, the profile value functions as an anchor rather than the operative sensitivity, and observed variable_sens spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit inversely tied to glucose, at 108.4 to 124.0 for 70-95 mg/dL and 37.9 and 27.8 at 245-262 mg/dL. Uncertainty: the fork uses non-stock dosing-sensitivity variants described as using eventual BG, using current BG and weighted on predicted BG due to delta, so the response of the effective sensitivity to a change in the anchor is not predictable from stock behaviour. Dependencies: the correct lever is the dynamic ISF adjustment factor, and changing both the anchor and the multiplier together would violate the rule against moving dependent parameters, so this stays fixed until the automation change has been evaluated.

Evidence: this target covers the 23:00-03:00 local window that carries 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, which argues for loosening, but the observed effective target_bg in that period includes 96.4, 97, 101, 104, 105 and 106 mg/dL rather than 90, so the profile value is not what the algorithm used. Uncertainty: the modulating logic is fork-level, seen in prTrial, twin and antBackout strings, and is undocumented in the package, so the transfer of a profile-target edit is unknown and could not be validated. Dependencies: the same window is better explained by the evening insulin tail, with 2.802 and 5.935 U on board at 22:04 and 22:09 local, which the primary automation change addresses first.

Evidence: the hours governed by this target are the safest in the dataset, with 0.0 percent below range at 08:00 and 09:00 local and 1.2 percent at 10:00, so there is no safety case for loosening and no hypoglycemia case for tightening. Uncertainty: observed target_bg values in the day range from 80 to 116 mg/dL, so the effective daytime target is not this value. Dependencies: none requiring a change, and this row is stable and serves as a useful fixed reference while the automation change is evaluated.

Evidence: 23:00 and 00:00 local show 11.4 and 18.5 percent below range on the following hour boundary, which suggests this tight target is unhelpful, but the observed effective targets differ from the profile and the dip recovers spontaneously to 106.0 mg/dL by 04:00 local without carbohydrate, pointing to an insulin tail rather than the target. Uncertainty: fork-level target modulation makes the effect of an edit unpredictable. Dependencies: kept so that only one insulin-affecting change is in flight, and if evening lows persist after the dynamic ISF change a modest overnight target loosening becomes a reasonable second discussion.

Evidence: the long tail is directly measurable, with 360-minute changes of -176, -173, -70, -68 and -66 mg/dL after small doses, and it is central to the mechanism linking afternoon dosing to evening lows. Uncertainty: insulin_type is free_peak_oref and no peak time is supplied, so DIA appropriateness can only be bounded rather than quantified, and a longer DIA with a correct peak is also the conservative setting for this algorithm family because it improves insulin-on-board accounting rather than degrading it. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change insulin-on-board accounting for every dose simultaneously and would confound the dynamic ISF evaluation, so it is withheld and the amplitude problem is addressed at the sensitivity layer instead.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrates logged and COB 0 in every sampled cycle, UAM is the only mechanism responding to the afternoon rises and to the 285-293 mg/dL excursions on 08-15 and 08-18, and overall time in range is 86.0 percent, so disabling either switch is unsupported. Uncertainty: the magnitude of UAM dosing is problematic even though the switches themselves are appropriate, since a 1.6 U SMB was recorded during UAM High Boost on 08-19 with 4.73 U already on board. Dependencies: the magnitude issue is handled by the dynamic ISF change rather than by these switches, and both source components have non-null values so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: the group is internally consistent, since smb_always_enabled true supersedes the COB and after-carbs conditions and with zero carbohydrate entries those two are inert rather than contradictory, while smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false is observably protective during the 180-minute 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18 that fall in the pre-hypoglycemia window. Uncertainty: 08-18 still recorded 12.8 percent below range despite that protection, consistent with a pre-existing insulin tail rather than SMB delivered during the temporary target. Dependencies: if carbohydrate logging begins, SMB will remain active because smb_always_enabled is true, so this group should be re-read then, but no change is supported now and all five components have non-null values so verify is not applicable.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: reducing max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 to 15 is a genuine candidate, since 20 UAM minutes at the current 0.7-0.8 U/h basal is roughly 0.23-0.27 U and the UAM window carries the severe lows, but it is withheld now for two reasons. First, dependency, because it targets the same over-delivery pathway as the primary dynamic ISF change and moving both together would make neither evaluable. Second, weak transfer, because the configured caps are demonstrably overridden by fork boost logic, with standardMaxBolus 0.2 followed by Microbolusing 0.4U on 08-07 and SMB equals 1.6 during UAM High Boost on 08-19, while the larger channel is temporary basal at 2.376 to 4.0 U/h against a 0.5-0.8 U/h schedule. Uncertainty: the boost thresholds are absent from the package, so the effective ceiling is unknown. smb_interval_minutes of 3 is the standard minimum and no snapshot contradicts it, and remaining-time text in SMB waiting messages was not treated as the configured interval. Dependencies: this is the designated second lever if evening time below range remains above 4 percent after the sensitivity change, and all three components are non-null so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: neither limit binds. The operative basal ceiling is about 4 U/h, produced by max_daily_safety_multiplier 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier 6, as shown by the 08-14 reason reading adj. req. rate 5.9 to maxSafeBasal 4, temp 3.60 below 4 U/hr and by the 08-21 rate capping at 4, so the configured 12 U/h is inert and lowering it would fight the multipliers rather than the cause. Peak observed insulin-on-board is 5.935 U against a 25 U cap, so that limit has never been approached and would not have prevented any observed event. Uncertainty: 25 U is high relative to this user's insulin exposure of 275.95 U over 14 days and is a weak backstop, but the package does not allow the basal and bolus split to be determined, so a defensible replacement value cannot be derived here. Dependencies: changing a non-binding backstop now would add a second concurrent change and risk being credited with an improvement it did not cause, so revisit only after the sensitivity change has been evaluated, and both components are non-null so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: this is the only group where a quantified mechanism links directly to the dominant safety finding. The 70 percent adjustment factor produces observed variable sensitivity of 27.8 and 37.9 mg/dL per unit at 245-262 mg/dL versus 108.4, 111.9 and 124.0 at 70-95 mg/dL, a 4.5-fold range around the flat 56 mg/dL per unit anchor, so the loop is most aggressive exactly when glucose is highest and then cannot brake for the following six hours under a 10-hour DIA. The consequences are documented, since 0.2 U at 14:05 local on 08-13 produced 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes, 0.2 U at 17:20 local on 08-14 produced 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes before the 41 mg/dL cluster, 0.65 U at 16:55 local on 08-19 with 4.73 U on board produced a 120-minute change of -168 mg/dL, and min_guard_bg values of -4, -59 and 28 mg/dL show the prediction floor being tested. Reducing the factor by one conservative step from 70 to 60 percent compresses the high-glucose end of the range and lowers total exposure, which is the only direction permitted while time below range is 5.1 percent. The four other components in this group are kept, since autosens_enabled false with dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true is a coherent standard pairing and the observed sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.0 are read as neutral or mildly reduced current adjustments rather than as evidence that Autosens is active. Uncertainty: the fork applies undocumented boost and target logic so the response magnitude cannot be predicted and must be observed, GLP-1 dosing every three days and the 08-19 occlusion overlap the evaluation window, and some increase in afternoon time above range should be expected. Dependencies: no other insulin-delivery parameter may be changed in the same period, and the UAM SMB minute reduction is explicitly held as the next lever.

Evidence: both parameters govern COB decay and COB duration and neither has been exercised once in 14 days, since carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty, extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null and COB is 0 in every sampled cycle. No pattern in the package can support or refute either value, and no e-carb duration is inferred from any aggregate average. Uncertainty: correctness is unknown, so this is a keep on untestability rather than on demonstrated accuracy. Dependencies: these become live and measurable only if carbohydrate logging begins as proposed in the observation-only recommendation, and both components are non-null so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: local hours 00 to 03 show means of 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL, which are normal, alongside time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent. Normal means with high time below range indicate residual insulin action rather than an excessive baseline rate, because a genuinely over-set basal would depress the mean as well. Uncertainty: no per-hour IOB series exists to test the residual insulin hypothesis directly, and loop rate samples are too sparse to reconstruct delivered basal. Dependencies: the same overnight lows are candidate evidence for the 10-hour DIA tail, for boost-scaled evening SMB and for dynamic ISF, none of which are separated, so a basal reduction here could remove baseline insulin that is not the cause.

Evidence: local hour 05 shows a mean of 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent below range and zero time above range, which is within target. This falls inside the cleanest window of the dataset. Uncertainty: the 4.8 percent below-range figure is the highest in the 04:00 to 08:00 block and may reflect the tail of overnight residual insulin rather than this segment. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; any adjustment here should wait until the overnight residual insulin question is resolved by the maximum IOB observation window.

Evidence: local hours 06, 07 and 08 show means of 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with time in range of 97.5, 98.7 and 98.2 percent, time below range of 2.5, 1.3 and 0.0 percent and time above range of 0.0, 0.0 and 1.8 percent. This is the best-controlled block in the entire period and is the strongest evidence in the package that basal magnitude is broadly appropriate. Uncertainty: the 42 mg/dL reading at 06:19 UTC on 08-21 falls in this window but occurred about 2.8 hours before a sensor change, so end-of-session inaccuracy is a live alternative explanation and it is not weighted as full evidence. Dependencies: none. This segment is the reference against which other windows are judged.

Evidence: local hour 10 has the second-highest daily mean at 148.0 mg/dL with 20.2 percent time above range and only 1.2 percent below range, following a climb from 110.5 at 08:00 and 132.9 at 09:00. Uncertainty: with zero carbohydrate entries across 14 days, an unannounced morning meal is at least as plausible an explanation as a basal shortfall, and the 08-14 window showing a rise of 88 mg/dL in 60 minutes from a starting value of 100 mg/dL has the shape of a meal rather than of insufficient baseline. Dependencies: raising basal here while time below range is 5.1 percent overall and while boost-scaled SMB delivery is unresolved would risk adding insulin to a system already reaching 5.935 U IOB. Carbohydrate logging is the prerequisite for evaluating this segment.

Evidence: local hour 16 carries the highest hourly mean of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent time above range and zero percent below range, while this segment sets the lowest daytime basal rate, so the profile shape is inverted relative to the observed curve at this hour. Uncertainty: this hour sits at the peak of a broad 12:00 to 17:00 plateau with no discrete onset and zero declared carbohydrate, so unannounced afternoon eating is the leading explanation; separately, 180-minute temporary targets at 135 mg/dL on 08-17 and 08-18 deliberately suppressed SMB inside this window, meaning the same hourly statistic has at least two distinct causes on different days. Dependencies: this segment feeds directly into the 18:00 and 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster, so any increase here could deepen the largest existing safety problem. Carbohydrate logging must separate the causes first.

Evidence: local hour 18 shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL and a falling mean of 124.2 mg/dL, and the profile raises basal from 0.5 to 0.6 U/h entering this hour, which is the direction opposite to the observed risk. Uncertainty: the descent into this hour is dominated by post-peak insulin arriving late, evidenced by 0.2 U at 234 mg/dL on 08-14 producing minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes, a drop the logged dose alone cannot produce, and by temp basal reaching the 4.0 U/h safe ceiling. A basal reduction of 0.1 U/h removes roughly 0.1 U per hour, which is negligible against boost-scaled SMB of 1.6 U. Dependencies: the maximum IOB change targets the same descent through a mechanism that matches its magnitude, and moving both would make attribution impossible. This segment becomes the next candidate only if the evening lows persist after that observation window.

Evidence: local hour 19 is the single worst hypoglycemia hour of the period at 15.3 percent time below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the profile raises basal again from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h entering it. Uncertainty: as with the 18:00 segment, the magnitude of the observed descents far exceeds what a 0.1 U/h basal difference could produce, and the two deepest level 2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 both followed large afternoon corrections rather than a steady baseline excess; 08-14 also had a GLP-1 dose that morning, which weakens it as evidence for any settings change. Dependencies: same as the 18:00 segment. Holding this row preserves clean attribution for the maximum IOB observation window, after which this segment and the 18:00 segment become the leading joint candidate for one small reduction, tested alone.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was declared at any point in the 14-day period, carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0 and cob was 0 in every sampled loop status, so this carb ratio has never been exercised and no observational basis exists to change it. A minor consistency observation is that loop reason strings report 13.3 g/U in this local segment against the profile value of 13.0, seen on 08-16 and 08-19, an offset of roughly 2 percent that may reflect dynamic carb ratio behavior, profile percentage or unit rounding. Uncertainty: that offset is small and its cause is not exposed in the package. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is the prerequisite for evaluating any carb ratio; until then a change would be pure speculation.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was declared during the period, so this segment has never acted on a meal. The loop reason string on 08-09 at 03:01 UTC, which is 04:01 local, reports CR 11.1, matching the profile exactly and confirming the segment boundary is applied in local time. Uncertainty: consistency confirmation is not effectiveness validation; a matching value says nothing about whether 11.1 g/U doses a meal correctly. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is required before any carb ratio can be assessed.

Evidence: this segment covers the mid-morning rise pattern where local hourly means climb from 110.5 at 08:00 to 148.0 at 10:00 with 20.2 percent time above range, but it is never invoked because carb_entries is 0, so those rises are handled entirely by UAM rather than by this carb ratio. Loop reason strings report CR 13.2 in this local window, matching the profile. Uncertainty: the morning rise could be caused by an unannounced meal, by the dawn-period basal, or by both, and these are not separated. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging for the morning meal is the prerequisite; this is the second-highest-value segment to validate after the afternoon one.

Evidence: this is the strongest carb ratio to have doses the afternoon plateau that peaks at local 16:00 with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent time above range, yet it is never invoked because no carbohydrate is declared. Loop reason strings report CR 10.5 in this local window, matching the profile. Uncertainty: because the plateau is slow and has no discrete onset, even a correct carb ratio would need appropriate meal timing to help, and no timing data exists. Dependencies: this is the single highest-value segment for the recommended carbohydrate logging, because validating it would simultaneously separate the unannounced-meal explanation from the dynamic ISF and basal shape explanations for the afternoon block.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was declared in this or any other window. Loop reason strings report CR 12.6 in this local segment, matching the profile. Local hours 20 and 21 are among the better-controlled evening hours with means of 117.0 and 120.0 mg/dL and time in range of 88.6 and 92.3 percent. Uncertainty: the absence of any exercised meal means the value is untested. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is required before assessment; no evidence in this window suggests any problem.

Evidence: this flat single-segment value is not the sensitivity actually applied, because dynamic_sensitivity_enabled is true with an adjustment factor of 70 percent, and sampled variable_sens ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U with a median near 79, falling monotonically as glucose rises. Uncertainty: the direction of any correction is genuinely ambiguous, since operational sensitivity is roughly half the profile value at high glucose and roughly double it at low glucose, so raising or lowering the anchor would help one end of the range and worsen the other. Dependencies: this is the critical one. Dynamic ISF is mathematically anchored to this value and to total daily dose, so the flat ISF and the 70 percent factor cannot be evaluated separately in this package and must never be moved in the same cycle. Moving this row now would also permanently confound the maximum IOB observation. If the first two changes do not reduce evening and overnight time below range, this row or the dynamic ISF factor becomes the next candidate, and only one of them may move.

Evidence: local hours 00 to 07 show acceptable means from 90.6 to 106.0 mg/dL, so the configured target is not producing elevated glucose, but time below range in hours 00 to 03 runs from 10.1 to 18.5 percent. Uncertainty: the configured value cannot be validated because sampled loop target_bg takes 13 distinct values from 80 to 116 mg/dL while both autosens target flags are false and logged temporary targets explain only part of the spread, meaning an undocumented build-specific mechanism is modulating the effective target. Dependencies: raising this target is a tempting response to the overnight lows, but the lows are better explained by residual insulin, and changing a target whose effective value is not reliably known would produce an uninterpretable result. The modulation rule should be clarified first.

Evidence: local hours 08 to 22 are covered by this segment and include both the best-controlled hour of the day at 08:00, with 98.2 percent time in range and zero percent below range, and the worst hyperglycemia block from 13:00 to 17:00. A single target cannot be blamed for both outcomes. Uncertainty: the same undocumented target modulation applies, and the recurring 80 mg/dL loop targets during the aggressive high-glucose episodes on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21 fall inside this segment, meaning the effective target during the riskiest moments is lower than configured for reasons not exposed in the package. Dependencies: clarification of the modulation rule is a prerequisite; until then any target change here has an unpredictable effective magnitude.

Evidence: local hour 23 shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with 88.7 percent time in range and 10.1 percent below range, so the mean is comfortable while the low exposure is elevated, which again matches residual insulin rather than a target that is set too low. Uncertainty: the undocumented target modulation applies here as it does to the other target rows. Dependencies: this row and the 00:00 target row govern the same overnight low cluster and would need to be considered together, which conflicts with the one-change-at-a-time rule while a better-matched and less entangled change, the maximum IOB ceiling, is available first.

Evidence: DIA is 10 hours with insulin_type free_peak_oref, and several response windows show effects persisting to 360 minutes, such as 0.05 U on 08-17 producing minus 34, minus 68 and minus 50 mg/dL at 2, 4 and 6 hours, and 08-19 showing minus 161 and minus 176 mg/dL at 4 and 6 hours. Uncertainty: this is evidence-blocked rather than merely uncertain. The insulin peak time is not supplied anywhere in the package, and every post-bolus decay window is contaminated by subsequent SMB delivery and temp basal activity, so it is impossible to determine whether the modelled tail is too fast or too slow relative to reality. Dependencies: DIA interacts with the 3-minute SMB interval and the multiplicative boosts to favour stacking, and peak IOB of 5.935 U is consistent with that interaction, but the maximum IOB ceiling addresses the same stacking risk with direct evidence. Changing DIA without a peak time and without one uncontaminated decay window would be speculative.

Evidence: both switches are enabled and consistent, and with carb_entries at 0 and cob at 0 in every sampled loop status, this pair is the only mechanism providing any meal coverage. Disabling either would remove all coverage of the local 13:00 to 17:00 block that reaches 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00. Aggregate outcomes of 86.0 percent time in range and 32.6 percent coefficient of variation indicate the framework itself is functioning. Uncertainty: the defect identified is dose magnitude from undocumented boost scaling, not the enable switches themselves. Dependencies: UAM is treated strictly as unannounced-rise detection and no duplicate COB counting is claimed, since cob is 0 throughout and no COB interaction is observable. Both source components carry non-null values, so verify is not admissible.

Evidence: the five flags are internally coherent. With smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, the frequent 135 mg/dL temporary targets logged on 08-09, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-20 act as a deliberate SMB off-switch, which is a purposeful defensive pattern. Under smb_always_enabled true, the smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled flags are effectively inert, and doubly so given zero carbohydrate entries. Uncertainty: the 180-minute temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18 suppressed SMB across part of the afternoon peak window and may contribute to afternoon time above range, but 08-18 also had 12.8 percent time below range and followed a site change, so the effects are not separable. Dependencies: enabling smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled would increase hypoglycemia exposure against the binding 5.1 percent time below range constraint and is therefore not supported. All five components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
rationale: Evidence: the configured minute caps reconcile exactly with reported standardMaxBolus values, with 15 minutes against 0.7 to 0.8 U/h giving 0.175 to 0.20 U against a reported 0.2, and 20 minutes against 0.8 U/h giving 0.267 U against a reported 0.3. However these caps form only the base of the dose and are then multiplied by UAM Boost 1 between 0.68 and 1.34, UAM Boost 2 between 0.24 and 35.93, and a UAM High Boost path, so on 08-19 a nominal 0.167 U base against 0.5 U/h basal produced a stated SMB of 1.6 U. The specific inconsistency addressed here is that max_uam_smb_basal_minutes at 20 exceeds max_smb_basal_minutes at 15, permitting the less certain unannounced path a 33 percent larger base than the announced path, which is never used because no carbohydrate is declared. Aligning to 15 reduces the base by 25 percent and, because the boosts are multiplicative, scales boosted output proportionally. Uncertainty: if the true driver is dynamic ISF rather than the base, the reduction may be partially absorbed by larger boost factors and the effect may be small; the boost configuration itself is not exposed anywhere in the package. Dependencies: this acts on the same insulin delivery pathway as the maximum IOB ceiling, so it must follow a complete observation window on that change and must be moved alone. smb_interval_minutes is held at 3 as the configured minimum spacing, which was not confused with remaining-time text in reason strings, and no evidence isolates the interval as the driver. max_smb_basal_minutes is held at 15 as the reference the UAM path is being aligned to.

Evidence: max_iob_units of 25 U never bound during the period. Peak observed IOB was 5.935 U on 08-21 with variable_sens at 27.8 mg/dL/U and an insulin requirement of 2.12 U at 245 mg/dL, and 4.73 U on 08-19 with a stated SMB of 1.6 U. Both peaks immediately preceded the largest descents in the dataset, minus 176 and minus 168 mg/dL over six hours, and predicted minGuardBG reached minus 59 mg/dL on 08-16 and minus 4 mg/dL on 08-11 before 120-minute zero temps were issued. Against an estimated total daily dose bracketed at 30 to 36 U per day, 25 U is roughly 70 to 80 percent of daily insulin, so the last-resort brake is functionally absent. A ceiling near 8 U, roughly 25 percent of estimated daily dose, would have bound only in the two extreme episodes. Uncertainty: the estimated daily dose is a bracket because delivered temp basal volume is not summarized in the package, so the exact ceiling value is a care-team decision rather than a derived number; the trade-off is that a binding ceiling will occasionally withhold correction of a genuine high and can extend time above range. Dependencies: max_basal_u_per_hour is held at 12 U/h because it is provably inert, since the 08-14 reason string shows the request reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, which equals the maximum profile basal of 0.8 U/h times the max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5.0, so the 12 U/h value has never been reached and changing it would have no effect. This change is placed first in the sequence precisely because it alters no ISF, basal, target, SMB size or SMB timing in normal operation and therefore does not contaminate attribution of any later change. Both components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

Evidence: the combination is valid and non-conflicting, running one sensitivity engine rather than two, and both autosens target flags are consistently false with Autosens off. sensitivity_ratio is not stuck at 1, with observed values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and 1.0, confirming an active adjustment path where 1 is a neutral current adjustment rather than a disabled feature. This group is the strongest candidate mechanism for the crashes, because sampled variable_sens falls to 27.8 to 43.2 mg/dL/U above 170 mg/dL against a flat profile anchor of 56, driving insulin requirements of 1.98 to 2.59 U and rates to the 4.0 U/h ceiling. Uncertainty: the 70 percent factor is mathematically anchored to the profile ISF of 56 and to total daily dose, and the internal daily dose value used by the algorithm is not exposed, so the factor and the anchor cannot be evaluated separately within this package. Dependencies: changing the factor now would alter every dosing decision including the already hypoglycemia-prone overnight window and would permanently confound the profile ISF question that must still be resolved. The explicit revisit rule is that if the maximum IOB ceiling and the UAM base alignment do not reduce time below range at local hours 18, 19, 00 to 03, then either this factor or the profile ISF anchor becomes the next candidate, and only one of the two may move. All five components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

Evidence: these two parameters govern COB decay and meal absorption modelling, and neither has been exercised once during the period. carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty, extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is a genuine null, and cob is 0 in every sampled loop status. Uncertainty: there is no observational basis whatsoever to move either value, and no e-carb duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: these become tunable only once carbohydrate is declared, which is also the precondition for the meal strategy phase. A forward-looking feasibility note is that the configuration is already compatible with carbohydrate announcement, because smb_always_enabled true means SMB would continue regardless of COB, so smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false would not block dosing, and min_carbs_required_grams of 20 would gate only the COB-dependent path. Both components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 show averages of 90.6 to 106 mg/dL with time below range of 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, but the decline begins in the evening at 22:00 with 127.6 mg/dL falling through 105.7 at 23:00 and self-corrects from 04:00 under the same 0.6 U/h rate. Uncertainty: a basal that was genuinely excessive would not self-correct while the rate is unchanged, so the residual insulin tail from evening corrections is the better-supported explanation, supported by 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL preceding 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes on 08-17. Dependencies: coupled to the 10 hour duration of insulin action, to the dynamic sensitivity curve and to the pending insulin on board ceiling change, which must be observed first.

Evidence: 05:00 local shows an average of 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range and 4.8 percent below range, one of the best hours in the period. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment; the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 08-21 is isolated and coincides with a sensor change the same morning. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; this segment anchors the conclusion that overall basal magnitude is reasonable.

Evidence: hours 06:00 to 08:00 local show averages of 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with 97.5, 98.7 and 98.2 percent time in range and 0 to 2.5 percent below range under the highest scheduled rate in the profile. Uncertainty: low; this is the strongest-performing window in the dataset. Dependencies: none; no change is supportable against this performance.

Evidence: the rise begins here, with 10:00 local at 148.0 mg/dL and 20.2 percent above range, and 08:00 immediately before shows 0 percent below range and only 1.8 percent above range. Uncertainty: high, because the meal-shaped onset with zero announced carbohydrates makes detection lag at least as plausible as a basal deficit, and GLP-1 dosing on a three-day cadence may shift absorption. Dependencies: cannot be separated from unannounced-meal detection behaviour until one recurring meal is logged; raising this segment would also add insulin whose tail lands in the 18:00 to 20:00 low window.

Evidence: this is the lowest scheduled rate and it coincides with the daily peak of 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local with 32.1 percent above range and 0.0 percent below range, which superficially suggests under-dosing. Uncertainty: high, because four explanations remain unseparated, namely detection lag with zero announced carbohydrates, GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying, microbolus suppression during the 135 mg/dL temporary targets recorded on 08-17, 08-18 and 08-19, and infusion set effects including the 08-19 occlusion. Dependencies: any increase here delivers insulin whose action peaks in the 18:00 to 20:00 window, where time below range is 7.7 and 15.3 percent with two level 2 events; this must not be changed before the meal logging check and the ceiling changes.

Evidence: 18:00 local shows 124.2 mg/dL with 7.7 percent below range, and the segment steps up into the worst daytime low hour. Uncertainty: the lows here follow documented large falls such as 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14 and 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16, so the correction tail is better supported than the basal step as the cause. Dependencies: attribution requires observing the effect of the insulin on board ceiling change first; changing basal and a ceiling together would make the outcome uninterpretable.

Evidence: 19:00 local carries the highest daytime low burden at 15.3 percent below range with an average of 105.4 mg/dL and includes the level 2 cluster of 48, 41 and 41 mg/dL on 08-14. Uncertainty: this is the strongest candidate for a future basal reduction, but the same hour is reached by the tail of afternoon corrections, and the 08-14 event followed a 0.2 U correction at 234 mg/dL, so the driver is not yet isolated. Dependencies: must wait until the insulin on board ceiling and, if needed, the unannounced-meal microbolus cap have been observed; reducing basal first would risk masking the actual cause and could worsen the afternoon elevation.

Evidence: carbohydrate entries are zero, total carbohydrates are 0.0 g, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status, so this ratio was never used to compute a bolus. Uncertainty: total for the value itself; the segment is confirmed loaded because the profile ratios are echoed in loop reason strings. Dependencies: becomes assessable only after carbohydrates are logged for recurring meals; keep rather than change because the current value exists and no change is supportable.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists in the fourteen-day window, so this segment produced no observable dosing. Uncertainty: total; the 04:00 to 08:00 window is the best-performing period of the day but that reflects basal and fasting behaviour, not carbohydrate ratio performance. Dependencies: requires announced meals before any evaluation is possible.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries mean this segment was never exercised, even though the morning rise from 110.5 mg/dL at 08:00 to 148.0 at 10:00 falls inside it. Uncertainty: total for the ratio; the rise is attributable to unannounced-meal detection lag rather than to a carbohydrate ratio that was never applied. Dependencies: assessable only with logged morning carbohydrates.

Evidence: this is the tightest ratio in the profile and it covers the highest above-range hours, 16:00 at 32.1 percent and 17:00 at 22.6 percent, yet zero carbohydrate entries mean it never generated a bolus. Uncertainty: total; no inference about its correctness can be drawn from the afternoon elevation, which is a detection and automation pattern rather than a carbohydrate ratio outcome. Dependencies: this is the priority segment for the recommended single-meal logging check.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries; the evening lows in this window followed small corrections and their tails, not meal boluses, as shown by 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL on 08-17 preceding 68 mg/dL at 180 minutes and 57 at 240 minutes. Uncertainty: total for the ratio value. Dependencies: unlogged rescue carbohydrate in this window is a confounder that must be recorded before any evaluation.

Evidence: the declared flat value is not what is delivered, because dynamic sensitivity is enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor and the applied sensitivity ranged from 124.0, 111.9 and 108.4 mg/dL/U at glucose of 69.8, 95.1 and 84 mg/dL down to 42.5, 43.2, 39.99, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL/U at glucose from 135 to 246 mg/dL. Uncertainty: high, because this profile value acts as a scaling reference for the whole dynamic curve rather than as the direct correction factor, so a change would move both the weak normal-range response and the strong high-glucose response at once. Dependencies: tightly coupled to the dynamic sensitivity adjustment factor and to the boost behaviour; only one of these may be reopened later, and only if the low burden persists after the ceiling changes.

Evidence: the declared value is 90 mg/dL, but loop statuses show effective targets of 80, 84, 86, 87, 96.4 and higher, including values below the declared floor when no temporary target was recorded. Uncertainty: high, because Autosens is disabled and both Autosens target adjustment flags are false, so the deviation is not explained by any inventory setting and appears to be intentional variant behaviour. Dependencies: no target change can be validated from this package; the mechanism should be clarified with the care team before any target edit is considered.

Evidence: the declared daytime target of 100 mg/dL is conservative and appropriate given time below range of 5.1 percent, yet observed effective targets during daytime cycles included 80 mg/dL at 262 and 245 mg/dL and 116 mg/dL on a hypo-guard cycle. Uncertainty: high, because the delivered target is dynamically modulated in a risk-inverse direction that the declared schedule does not describe. Dependencies: raising the declared target might reduce afternoon dosing pressure, but with the effective target already overridden the outcome would be unpredictable, so no change is supportable.

Evidence: this segment covers the start of the late-evening decline, where 23:00 local averages 105.7 mg/dL with 10.1 percent below range. Uncertainty: high, because the observed lows in this window follow evening correction tails rather than target-driven dosing, and the effective target deviates from the declared value. Dependencies: any target discussion must follow clarification of the dynamic target mechanism and must not coincide with the ceiling or basal work.

Evidence: a 10 hour duration with a free peak insulin model is consistent with the observed long tails, where 0.05 U at 125 mg/dL preceded 68 mg/dL at 180 minutes and 57 at 240 minutes on 08-17, 0.15 U at 138 preceded 82 to 87 mg/dL on 08-12, and 0.05 U at 93 preceded 69 mg/dL on 08-10, since such small boluses cannot themselves cause those falls. Uncertainty: high, because no insulin on board time series was supplied to test the decay curve directly, and 10 hours may be the intended setting for this insulin model rather than an error. Dependencies: the duration interacts with the dynamic sensitivity curve and with the insulin on board ceiling; changing it alongside either would make attribution impossible, so it is held until the ceiling change has been observed.

Evidence: both components are non-null and enabled, and with zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrates on board zero in all supplied statuses, unannounced-meal detection is the entire meal-response system; disabling either would remove the only meal response. Uncertainty: the arrangement is reactive by construction, which sets a floor on afternoon time above range, but that is a strategy consequence rather than a misconfiguration, and unannounced-meal detection is not duplicating carbohydrate counting here. Dependencies: the reactive lag is best addressed by logging carbohydrates, not by disabling these switches; verify is not available because no component is null.

Evidence: always-enabled microbolusing supersedes the with-carbohydrates and after-carbohydrates switches, so those two are inert labels rather than active restrictions, which is a cosmetic inconsistency only. The materially active condition is that microbolusing is disabled during high temporary targets, which suppressed dosing during the 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 08-17, 08-18 and 08-19, all overlapping the highest above-range afternoon hours. Uncertainty: that suppression plausibly contributes to afternoon time above range on those specific days, but it is hypo-protective and the user appears to apply those targets deliberately, with no activity log available to confirm the reason. Dependencies: enabling microbolusing during high temporary targets would push against the dominant safety constraint of 5.1 percent time below range with two level 2 evening events, so no change is supportable; verify is not available because all five components are non-null.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: the unannounced-meal cap of 20 basal minutes exceeds the standard 15 basal minutes, and since carbohydrates are never announced the larger speculative cap is the only one that applies, which points the wrong way against 15.3 percent time below range at 19:00 local. The 3 minute interval is not the binding rate limiter because CGM cadence is 5.0 minutes and loop cycles follow the CGM. Uncertainty: high on effect size, because the variant delivered above the configured standard bolus cap in documented cycles, microbolusing 0.4 U against a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U on 08-07 and 1.6 U under a high boost on 08-19, so tightening the cap may achieve less than the setting implies. Dependencies: this changes routine delivery, unlike the ceilings, so it is deliberately deferred to a later separate round after the insulin on board ceiling has been observed; keep now rather than change so that no two dependent delivery settings move together.

Evidence: both ceilings are inert. The loop capped an adjusted request of 5.9 U/h at a maximum safe basal of 4 U/h on 08-14, so 12 U/h never bound anything and 4 U/h reproduces the ceiling already in force. The 25 U insulin on board limit exceeds a full day of insulin, given 275.95 U over fourteen days and a 16.2 U per day scheduled basal, while the highest observed insulin on board was 5.935 U at 245 mg/dL and 4.73 U at 262 mg/dL, both with zero carbohydrates on board; a limit of 8 U would therefore not have blocked any dosing observed in this period while bounding the accumulation that preceded 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 within 120 minutes on 08-19 and 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16. Uncertainty: the suggested values are candidates for care-team review, not prescriptions, and the appropriate insulin on board ceiling depends on the individual largest meal bolus plus basal accumulation, which cannot be derived here because no meal boluses exist in the data. Dependencies: none blocking, which is precisely why this is sequenced first; it is behaviourally neutral for the observed period and therefore creates a clean baseline before any delivery or profile change. The two components should still be introduced one at a time.

Evidence: the configuration is internally coherent, with one sensitivity path rather than two, and with Autosens off the target adjustment flags are correctly inert. A sensitivity ratio of 1 in most statuses is a neutral current adjustment and not evidence of anything disabled; the values 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 occur on hypo-guard cycles and are consistent with the dynamic path working. The delivered sensitivity nevertheless spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as strong as the profile value at high glucose and about half as strong in the normal range, which matches the observed slow climb and abrupt fall. Uncertainty: high and bidirectional, because lowering the adjustment factor would reduce the high-glucose over-correction and help the 5.1 percent time below range but would simultaneously weaken the already slow 100 to 150 mg/dL response and worsen the 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 local. Dependencies: coupled to the flat profile sensitivity of 56 mg/dL/U and to the boost behaviour, so three inputs feed one outcome; this may be reopened only after the ceiling change has been observed, and then only instead of, never together with, a profile sensitivity change. Verify is not available because all five components are non-null.

Evidence: both values are present and conventional, and both were inert for the entire period because carbohydrate entries are zero, extended carbohydrate entries are zero, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status, so neither parameter influenced a single dosing decision. Uncertainty: no observational basis exists to tune either value, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate, since the average extended carbohydrate duration field is null. Dependencies: relevance is blocked by the absence of carbohydrate logging rather than by any data-quality defect; this group becomes assessable only once meals are announced, so keep is used rather than change or verify, and verify is unavailable because both components are non-null.

Evidence: the 00:00 to 02:00 local hours carry the highest low-glucose exposure of the day at 18.5 and 10.1 percent, which superficially implicates this segment, but glucose recovers from a 90.6 mg/dL nadir at 01:00 to 101.9 at 02:00 and 104.7 at 03:00 while this same rate remains in force, and 03:00 to 05:00 shows only 3.0 and 4.8 percent below range. A fixed basal excess would produce continued decline rather than self-recovery. Sampled overnight temp basals swing both ways, including 0 U/h and 1.984 U/h, so the loop is not systematically suppressing this segment. Uncertainty: the temp basal sample is 30 records and is not duration-weighted, and no per-hour insulin on board series exists. Dependencies: the competing explanation is carry-over of evening insulin, which the maximum IOB change is designed to test; this segment must not be changed in the same window as that automation change.

Evidence: the 05:00 local hour shows 95.2 percent time in range with zero percent above range and 4.8 percent below range, and the surrounding 03:00 to 08:00 block is the best-controlled part of the day. There is no directional signal supporting either an increase or a decrease. Uncertainty: the modest 4.8 percent low exposure could reflect residual overnight insulin rather than this segment. Dependencies: protected by the safety constraint that no proposal may increase net insulin between 19:00 and 03:00 local, and by the decision to keep the adjacent 00:00 segment unchanged so that any future signal remains attributable.

Evidence: the 06:00 and 07:00 local hours show 97.5 and 98.7 percent time in range with zero percent above range and 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range, the strongest control of any window, indicating this dawn rate is well matched. Uncertainty: a single 42 mg/dL extreme was recorded at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21, but one event within a window of 98.7 percent time in range does not establish a segment defect and could reflect residual insulin or sensor behaviour. Dependencies: none that would justify change; this segment is explicitly protected in the implementation order.

Evidence: the 09:00 to 11:00 local rise from 132.9 to 148.0 to 132.3 mg/dL crosses the 0.8 to 0.7 step and reaches 20.2 percent above range at 10:00, but low exposure is only 0 to 1.2 percent, and with zero carbohydrate entries an unannounced eating occasion is at least as plausible an explanation as a basal defect. A pattern is not labelled a profile defect while meals remain a plausible cause. Uncertainty: the rise cannot be separated from food without carbohydrate logging. Dependencies: resolution depends on the carbohydrate logging observation; only after announced meals exist can this segment be assessed.

Evidence: the 16:00 local hour is the worst of the day at 162.8 mg/dL average with 32.1 percent above range, and this is the lowest basal segment, which superficially suggests it is too low. This is not adopted because the following hours fall to 124.2 and 105.4 with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range, showing that afternoon insulin does arrive and does so in excess and late. Raising this segment would most plausibly deepen the evening lows and would violate the safety constraint against increasing insulin before 19:00 to 03:00 exposure is resolved. Uncertainty: the afternoon highs are strongly confounded by unannounced eating and by GLP-1 dosing on three days. Dependencies: this segment can only be reassessed after carbohydrate logging separates meal effects from basal effects.

Evidence: the 18:00 local hour shows 7.7 percent below range with 11.9 percent above range and an average of 124.2 mg/dL, a mixed picture in which glucose is descending steeply from the afternoon peak. The low exposure here is attributed to insulin delivered earlier at the peak rather than to this basal rate, since a 0.2 U logged bolus preceded a 178 mg/dL fall on 2026-08-14 that the dose cannot explain at any sensitivity in the observed range. Uncertainty: a small contribution from this segment cannot be excluded without a duration-weighted temp basal series. Dependencies: attribution rests on the stacking hypothesis being tested by the maximum IOB change; reassess only afterwards.

Evidence: the 19:00 local hour carries 15.3 percent below range with an average of 105.4 mg/dL and minimum of 41 mg/dL, the second worst low window of the day, and this segment steps up from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h. A reduction is nonetheless withheld because the observed falls are far larger than any basal rate could produce, with two windows showing 168 and 178 mg/dL drops in 120 minutes following 0.65 U and 0.2 U logged boluses, indicating automated delivery rather than basal as the driver. Changing basal now would confound the maximum IOB observation. Uncertainty: this is the profile segment with the strongest residual case for a future reduction if the automation change proves insufficient. Dependencies: explicitly queued as the next candidate after the maximum IOB change is evaluated, as a single isolated change.

Evidence: no carbohydrate has been logged in fourteen days, with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0 and COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status, so this segment has no supporting or refuting evidence. A roughly 2 percent offset was noted between this profile value and the value 13.3 appearing in loop reason strings within this window, which is too small and too uncertain in origin to act on. Uncertainty: complete. The 24 therapy response windows are all correction boluses and cannot be used to derive a carb ratio, as shown by 0.2 U doses producing 120-minute changes from plus 77 to minus 178 mg/dL. Dependencies: unblocked only by the carbohydrate logging observation.

Evidence: this value was confirmed as active by loop reason strings reporting CR 11.1 at local times within this segment, which validates that the profile is running, but zero carbohydrate entries mean the value itself is unvalidated for adequacy. Uncertainty: complete with respect to correctness. Dependencies: assessment requires logged carbohydrates within the 04:00 to 08:00 local window, which do not exist; no change may be inferred from correction bolus behaviour.

Evidence: this segment covers the 09:00 to 11:00 local rise where an unannounced eating occasion is most strongly suspected, and the value was confirmed active in loop reason strings. However, with zero carbohydrate entries there is no basis to judge whether 13.2 g/U is correct. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: this is the highest-priority segment to unblock, and it is the specific target of the recommended carbohydrate logging observation for the eating occasion preceding the 09:00 to 11:00 rise.

Evidence: this is the most aggressive carb ratio in the profile and it spans the worst hyperglycaemia hour at 16:00 and the worst evening low hour at 19:00, but it is entirely inactive in practice because no carbohydrate has ever been entered, so it has contributed nothing to the observed pattern. Uncertainty: complete with respect to correctness; certain with respect to non-involvement in the observed data. Dependencies: relevant only if carbohydrate logging begins in the afternoon window, at which point its aggressiveness should be reviewed against the existing evening low pattern before use.

Evidence: confirmed active in loop reason strings at local times within this segment, but unvalidated because no carbohydrate has been logged. This segment overlaps the 22:00 to 03:00 low window, where five correction windows drifted low by 180 to 240 minutes, but those were corrections and not meal boluses, so they carry no information about this carb ratio. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: any future use in this window must account for the existing overnight low pattern and the carry-over mechanism under test.

Evidence: with dynamic sensitivity enabled and Autosens disabled, this flat value functions as a seed rather than the operative sensitivity. Observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, so effective insulin action is weaker than 56 near target and roughly twice as strong at 245 to 262 mg/dL. Changing the seed would be non-linearly rescaled by dynamic ISF, most strongly at the high end where the falls that produced lows originated. Uncertainty: the exact relationship between this seed and variable sensitivity in this modified fork is unconfirmed. Dependencies: this parameter and dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent are mutually confounding and must never be changed together; both are held while the maximum IOB change is evaluated first.

Evidence: the declared 90 mg/dL cannot be treated as the operative target, because effective targets observed in loop statuses ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL while both autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target are false, and user temporary targets explain only part of that range. Raising this target is a plausible response to the 18.5 percent low exposure at 01:00 local, but it cannot be justified while the algorithm is modulating targets independently and while the carry-over hypothesis is untested. Uncertainty: high, because the source of the autonomous target modulation is undocumented fork logic. Dependencies: revisit only after the maximum IOB change, and only if overnight low exposure persists.

Evidence: this daytime target spans both the 13:00 to 18:00 high block and the 18:00 to 20:00 low block, so no single directional change would improve both. Observed effective targets within this period included 80, 87, 99, 104, 106, 108 and 116 mg/dL, confirming the declared value is not what the algorithm used. Uncertainty: high; the same undocumented target modulation applies. Dependencies: any target discussion is subordinate to resolving the timing of afternoon insulin, which depends on the carbohydrate logging observation.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows 88.7 percent time in range with 10.1 percent below range and only 1.2 percent above range, and glucose is already descending from the evening. This is consistent with carried-over insulin rather than with the target value itself, since the descent begins before this segment starts. Uncertainty: a higher overnight target is a reasonable future safety lever, but it cannot be separated from the carry-over mechanism at present. Dependencies: assess only after the maximum IOB change, and never simultaneously with a basal or ISF change.

Evidence: 10 hours is long, but it is not refutable from these data and it is not implicated in the observed lows. Several therapy response windows show meaningful change at 360 minutes, including minus 176, minus 70 and minus 66 mg/dL, which is weakly consistent with long action, though every one of those windows is confounded by concurrent temp basal and unannounced food. Mechanistically a long DIA raises computed insulin on board, which restrains rather than increases dosing. Uncertainty: high, because the insulin peak time for the free_peak_oref insulin type is absent from the package, so the insulin on board curve cannot be reconstructed. Dependencies: shortening DIA would raise apparent dosing headroom and would directly counteract the maximum IOB guardrail, so it must not be changed alongside it.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB reported as 0 in every sampled status, UAM is the sole meal-handling mechanism and is delivering 86.0 percent time in range on entirely unannounced eating. UAM is treated strictly as unannounced-rise detection; because COB is always 0, no duplicate carbohydrate counting can occur and none is assumed. Disabling either switch would convert the 13:00 to 18:00 block, already at 22.6 to 32.1 percent above range, into a substantially larger one. Uncertainty: both components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the residual uncertainty concerns the fork boost logic layered on top, not these switches. Dependencies: all SMB sizing and stacking questions are handled through the delivery and safety limit groups rather than by disabling the mechanism.

Evidence: the group is internally coherent. smb_always_enabled true logically dominates the two carbohydrate-conditional switches, and with zero carbohydrates those switches are inert rather than contradictory. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false meaningfully suppresses SMB during the five recorded 135 mg/dL temporary targets, including two 180-minute windows on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, and this is a coherent manual brake consistent with the crash history rather than a defect. Uncertainty: all five components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the suppression behaviour means those two afternoons must be excluded from SMB sizing evidence. Dependencies: if carbohydrate logging begins, the carbohydrate-conditional switches and the 20 gram minimum become live and should be reviewed then, before any change here.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: both caps are already below AAPS defaults of 30 and 30, and the 3-minute interval matches the 5-minute CGM cadence appropriately. The caps reconcile arithmetically with the data, yielding roughly 0.23 U at 0.7 U/h basal against a reported standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U, and 0.27 U at 0.8 U/h against a reported 0.3 U. However, they are not the operative ceiling: one status delivered 0.4 U against a 0.2 U standard maximum and another delivered 1.6 U under UAM High Boost, with boost multipliers observed from 0.24 to 35.93. Reducing the UAM cap from 20 to 15 would scale only the boost base and would carry a clear cost against the existing 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 with zero percent below range in that hour. Uncertainty: all three components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the effect size of any cap change is unpredictable because fork boost logic overrides it. Dependencies: this is the third-ranked stacking limiter and must be considered only after the maximum IOB change has been observed for a full window, never simultaneously with it or with the dynamic ISF factor.

suggested_value: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h unchanged; max_iob_units reduced from 25 U to a care-team-agreed ceiling clearly above routine operating IOB and far below 25 U, for example in the region of 8 to 10 U if total daily dose is confirmed near 20 U per day
rationale: Evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is non-binding and is left unchanged, because the effective ceiling comes from the daily safety product, shown by a status reporting an adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, with the highest enacted rate anywhere in the sample being 3.6 U/h. max_iob_units of 25 is the weak link: profile basal is 16.2 U per day and total_insulin_u averages 19.7 U per day, so 25 U permits approximately a full day of insulin to be simultaneously active. Sampled peaks reached 4.73 U immediately before a fall from 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes, and 5.935 U at 245 mg/dL while a further 2.12 U was still being requested at a variable sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit. This bounds the stacking mechanism implicated in the 18:00 to 20:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 low windows without altering routine dosing. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 statuses were sampled so 5.935 U is a floor rather than a true peak, and it is unresolved whether total_insulin_u includes basal delivery, which changes estimated total daily dose between roughly 20 and 36 U per day and therefore the appropriate ceiling; the exact value must be set by the care team against the actual total daily dose. Dependencies: this is ranked first precisely because it is the only stacking limiter adjustable without confounding basal, ISF, target or SMB sizing; it must not be combined with the dynamic ISF factor, the UAM cap, or any profile change.

Evidence: the group is internally consistent. An earlier inference in this analysis, that non-unity sensitivity ratios of 0.79 to 0.98 proved hidden Autosens activity, is withdrawn: with dynamic sensitivity enabled those ratios arise from the dynamic sensitivity path, and a ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment rather than evidence of disabled Autosens. Dynamic ISF is the de facto sensitivity engine, with observed variable sensitivity spanning 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile seed of 56. A reduction of the adjustment factor would act as a global gain reduction, weakening insulin at every glucose level, and would be expected to worsen the existing 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 while only partially addressing the lows, because the timing analysis indicates insulin arrives late rather than being excessive in total. Uncertainty: all five components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the direction and implementation of the adjustment factor in this modified fork is unconfirmed, which is an additional reason to withhold. Dependencies: mutually confounding with the profile ISF seed and with the maximum IOB change; revisit only after carbohydrate logging has produced 7 to 10 days of announced meals so that timing and gain can be separated.

Evidence: both parameters act on COB decay and deviation accounting, and COB was reported as 0 in every sampled loop status across fourteen days with zero grams of carbohydrate logged, so they are functionally inert in this dataset and no evidence can support a change. Both values have concrete current values, so keep is used rather than any missing-data status and verify is not permissible. One forward-looking observation is recorded rather than acted on: every observed unannounced rise rate, between 1.6 and 7.3 mg/dL per 5 minutes, sits below the 8 mg/dL threshold, so if carbohydrate logging begins, COB would be assumed to decay faster than real absorption appears to proceed.
