Uncertainty: the rise rates were derived from correction bolus windows confounded by insulin action, so they are indicative only and not a measurement of carbohydrate absorption. Dependencies: this group becomes evaluable only after the carbohydrate logging observation produces non-zero COB, and it should be re-checked before, not alongside, any extended carbohydrate use.

The 00:00-05:00 local block shows time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent at hours 23, 1, 2 and 3 local with means of 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL and spontaneous recovery by 04:00, which is a real pattern. However, the evidence does not separate three competing causes: an insulin tail under the 10-hour DIA, the 0.6 U/h basal itself, and the tight 90 mg/dL target that leaves no buffer. Delivered temp basal in this window ranged from 0 to nearly 2 U/h in the sample, so the hourly average does not measure the scheduled rate. Uncertainty is further raised by IOB peaks of 2.80 and 5.935 U late in the evening. This segment is dependent on the outcome of the UAM delivery change and cannot be adjusted at the same time.

The 05:00-06:00 local window performs well, with a mean of 104.2 mg/dL, 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent time below range and no time above range. There is no evidence of a defect, and any change here would risk the best-controlled part of the day. Uncertainty is low for this segment; the only caveat is that the isolated 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local on 08-21 sits nearby, which is monitored rather than acted upon. No dependency requires a change.

The 06:00-10:00 local block is the strongest of the day, with means of 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL and time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2 and 91.1 percent, with time below range of 2.5, 1.3, 0.0 and 0.0 percent. This segment is validated by the data and should be preserved as a reference for the rest of the analysis. The only uncertainty is that the 09:00-10:00 local rise begins here and may be meal-related, which cannot be resolved without carbohydrate entries.

The 10:00-16:00 local block shows rising means from 148.0 to 162.8 mg/dL with time above range from 20.2 to 32.1 percent, which could suggest insufficient basal. However, carb_entries is 0 and COB is 0 in all sampled statuses, so unannounced meals are at least as plausible, and delivered temp basal in this window reached 2.7 to 4.0 U/h, several times the scheduled rate, which means the loop was not constrained by this segment. Raising basal here would also add insulin upstream of the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster, which is the opposite of the current safety priority. Dependent on carbohydrate visibility and on the UAM change before reassessment.

This segment coincides with the worst hyperglycemia of the day, 162.8 mg/dL mean and 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00 local, while carrying the lowest scheduled rate of the profile, which makes it the most tempting change in the package. It is withheld for three reasons: unannounced meals explain the same rise with zero carbohydrate entries, the loop already overrode this segment with temp basals up to 4.0 U/h and was clamped at maxSafeBasal on 08-14, and increasing insulin here would feed directly into the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. It is also the segment most likely to have been set low deliberately for unrecorded afternoon activity. This is the highest-priority profile candidate for reassessment once the UAM change and carbohydrate logging are in place.

This segment adds basal into a falling limb: means drop from 148.9 to 124.2 mg/dL at 18:00 local with 7.7 percent time below range and a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and two of the three level-2 episodes occur at 18:00-19:15 local. A reduction is therefore directionally plausible. It is withheld because the leading explanation is the insulin tail from afternoon UAM dosing under a 10-hour DIA rather than the scheduled 0.6 U/h, evidenced by falls of 178 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.2 U, and because changing this segment simultaneously with the UAM delivery change would make neither effect interpretable. This is the second profile candidate for reassessment if the evening hypoglycemia persists after the automation step.

The 19:00 local hour carries the highest time below range of the entire day at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, while the scheduled basal rises to its joint-highest daytime value. This is a genuine mismatch in direction. The change is withheld for the same reason as the 18:00 segment: the 08-14 sequence of 234 to 200 to 56 mg/dL after a 0.2 U dose shows automation, not scheduled basal, driving the fall, and the two settings must not be changed together. If the evening cluster survives the UAM reduction, this segment and the 18:00 segment become the primary review targets, one at a time.

This carb ratio was never exercised during the period: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so the value appears only as profile read-back inside loop reason strings. There is no evidence in either direction, so keep is the correct status rather than any change. Dependent on carbohydrate logging becoming available before any assessment is possible.

No carbohydrate was entered at any time in the 14-day window, so this segment produced no dosing and cannot be validated or refuted. The 04:00-08:00 local window is in any case the best-controlled part of the day on basal alone. Keep, dependent on future carbohydrate entries.

Unvalidatable for the same reason: zero carbohydrate entries and COB 0 throughout mean this ratio never contributed insulin. The morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between 08:00 and 10:00 local was handled entirely by UAM, so it carries no information about the carb ratio. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging.

This is the strongest carb ratio in the profile and covers the worst hyperglycemia block, but with zero carbohydrate entries it was never applied, so the 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00 local says nothing about its correctness. No change is supportable. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging for the recurring afternoon meal, which is the designated next observation.

Never exercised during the period, as with all other carb-ratio segments. The evening pattern in this window is dominated by the falling limb from the afternoon and by insulin tail effects, not by carbohydrate dosing. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging.

The single flat ISF segment is not used directly, because dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and rescaled the effective value across a 4.5-fold range from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit in the sampled statuses. This makes the profile ISF and the dynamic-ISF adjustment factor partially interchangeable levers on the same output, so changing this value now would confound the planned automation observation and it is explicitly excluded from being changed together with the sensitivity group. There is also a material safety consideration: at the terminal status, 5.935 U of IOB implies a fall of about 165 mg/dL at the dynamic value of 27.8 but about 332 mg/dL at the profile value of 56, so the correct choice between the two levers requires the post-change observation. Keep for now; this is the designated third decision point in the sequence.

A target of 90 mg/dL through the 00:00-08:00 local block is tight and coincides with 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent time below range in the first hours, which makes a small increase directionally plausible. It is withheld because the same overnight pattern is equally explained by the 10-hour insulin tail from evening automation, because the 04:00-08:00 portion of the same segment performs excellently at 95.2 to 98.7 percent time in range, and because a target change would alter loop behaviour at the same time as the planned UAM change. Dependent on the outcome of that observation.

The 100 mg/dL daytime target applies across both the best-performing morning hours and the worst afternoon hours, so the hourly data give no consistent signal about it. Effective targets in the sampled statuses already varied between 80 and 116 mg/dL, and the user applied 135 mg/dL temporary targets six times, which is a more flexible instrument than a standing target change and is already in use. No change is supportable; dependent on the automation observation.

The 23:00 local hour shows 11.4 percent time below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL, and this segment sets a 90 mg/dL target immediately before the deepest overnight cluster, so it is a plausible contributor. It is withheld because the cause is not separated from the insulin tail and the 0.6 U/h basal that begins one hour later, and because changing the target and the UAM strength together would be uninterpretable. This segment is reassessed together with the 00:00 basal segment after the automation observation.

A 10-hour DIA is long and is a plausible contributor to the prolonged declines observed at 240 to 360 minutes after very small doses, such as 125 to 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes and 75 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-17, and 206 to 53 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 08-16. However, those windows contain concurrent temp basal and microbolus delivery, so they demonstrate net system action rather than the insulin curve, and no insulin peak time is supplied in the package despite insulin_type free_peak_oref, so the DIA and peak pairing cannot be validated. A longer DIA is also conservative for IOB accounting, meaning a reduction could increase rather than decrease dosing. No change is supportable on this evidence; dependent on the peak time being clarified with the care team.

Both components are present and non-null, so verify is not applicable. With zero carbohydrate entries and COB 0 in every sampled status, UAM is the only mechanism covering meals, and disabling either switch would leave every rise uncovered and would predictably worsen the 13:00-17:00 local block that already runs at 16.6 to 32.1 percent time above range. The identified problem is delivery gain, not the existence of SMB or UAM, and the gain is addressed in the delivery group instead. Uncertainty is low for this decision; the dependency is that the delivery group change must be the one that carries the effect.

All five components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. The group is internally consistent: smb_always_enabled true currently supersedes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false, which are therefore inert while no carbohydrates are entered, and smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false gives the user a working manual brake that was used six times through 135 mg/dL temporary targets, including two 180-minute periods. No component change is supported by the data. The dependency to note is that the two currently inert flags become active as soon as carbohydrate logging begins, so this group must be re-examined at that point rather than assumed unchanged.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
rationale: Only one component is proposed for change: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 min to 15 min. Evidence: UAM is the sole meal-handling path, and observed microboluses exceeded the computed cap in this non-stock build, with 0.4 U delivered against a stated standardMaxBolus of 0.2 U under UAM Boost values of 1.23 and 1.57, and a high-boost microbolus of 1.6 U issued while IOB was already 4.73 U. Downstream consequences are falls of 178, 168 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.65 U or less, guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL with 120-minute zero temporary basals, IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U with COB 0, and evening time below range of 7.7 and 15.3 percent with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. Because the UAM minute setting scales the base that the boosts multiply, the change acts proportionally and specifically on the UAM path and leaves the excellent 04:00-08:00 local window largely untouched. Uncertainty: the build-specific boost multipliers are not documented in the package, so the magnitude is approximate and must be verified empirically, and afternoon time above range may increase. Dependencies: smb_interval_minutes of 3 min is never binding against a 5-minute CGM cadence and stays unchanged, max_smb_basal_minutes of 15 min governs the non-UAM path and stays unchanged, and this change must not be combined with any sensitivity, ISF, basal or target change.

Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable, and both are currently non-binding, which is exactly why changing them is safe and comes first. rationale: Evidence: the maximum insulin-on-board of 25 U is approximately 70 percent of the estimated total daily dose of about 36 U, calculated from a profile basal of 16.2 U/day plus roughly 19.7 U/day of bolus and SMB derived from 275.95 U over 14 days, while the highest observed insulin-on-board was 5.935 U on 08-21 at 22:09 local and the second highest 4.73 U on 08-19 at 16:54 local. The limit therefore never binds and provides no practical brake on the stacking that precedes the repeated high-to-low overshoots, including 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes and 264 mg/dL falling by 168 mg/dL in 120 minutes. Lowering it while retaining clear headroom above the observed maximum leaves routine dosing unchanged and creates an upper bound only in the extreme tail. The maximum basal component is kept because it is inert: the effective ceiling is 4 U/h produced by the maximum daily safety multiplier of 5 applied to the highest profile basal of 0.8 U/h, shown directly by a reason string adjusting a required rate of 5.9 down to a maximum safe basal of 4, so 12 U/h is a cosmetic inconsistency rather than an active risk. Uncertainty: this guardrail limits accumulated insulin but not the per-dose boost amplification, which is not exposed as a tunable, so it is a partial mitigation; the exact target value must be set by the care team. Dependencies: independent of the SMB delivery and sensitivity groups, which is why it can be changed alone and first. Both components are non-null so verify is not permitted.
